comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read AGENTS.md and skill playbooks
- [x] Check actionability (depends on #5995, several design choices unstated)
- [x] Survey existing zephyr skills and config surface
- [x] Post research + clarifying questions; no PR (design-sized, dep-blocked)

# Research

Two reasons this isn't PR-ready:

1. **Hard dep on #5995.** Bullet 2 ("use the stats from #5995") needs the `zephyr.stage` finelog stream from #5995, which isn't built yet — the proposed approach was just posted there today with open questions. A skill written against stats that don't exist will codify a fake schema. The skew-detection bullet has the same problem at per-shard granularity (`zephyr.shard`), and #5995's current scope explicitly defers per-shard rows.
2. **No definition of done for the skill itself.** The bullets describe *inputs to a heuristic*, not the skill's output, entry point, or scope. Concretely: where does the skill apply its recommendation (config file diff? new job submission? PR comment? chat reply?), what knobs does it touch (`map_workers_per_actor`, `reduce_workers_per_actor`, Iris `--memory`, scatter buffer fractions?), is it pre-job (plan from inputs only) or post-mortem (analyze a finished run) or mid-flight (suggest restart params)?

What's available today vs. what the skill would need:

| Need | Today | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Shard count from inputs | [`readers.py#L98`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/readers.py#L98) `InputFileSpec`; row/byte ranges already supported | None — can list/size files via gsutil/fsspec |
| Per-stage throughput | [`execution.py#L191-L241`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py#L191-L241) `_stage_throughput` (in-process only) | Needs #5995 to land for cross-run history |
| Per-shard skew signal | [`OPS.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/OPS.md) "Straggler Detection" — manual via `list-tasks` memoryMb + `actor call get_counters` | No durable per-shard counter stream (#5995 defers `zephyr.shard`) |
| Memory/thread knobs | [`execution.py#L1356`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py#L1356) `map_workers_per_actor` / `reduce_workers_per_actor`; Iris `--memory` on `job run` | None |

**Relevant code**
- [`readers.py#L98-L125`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/readers.py#L98-L125) — `InputFileSpec`, the natural shard unit
- [`execution.py#L1356-L1416`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py#L1356-L1416) — worker-slot knobs the skill would tune
- [`shuffle.py#L138-L142`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/shuffle.py#L138-L142) — scatter buffer is `memory / num_workers`, so memory and worker-count tune together
- [`OPS.md` — Straggler Detection / Data Skew](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/zephyr/OPS.md) — already documents the manual procedure a skill would automate
- [`.agents/skills/babysit-zephyr/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.agents/skills/babysit-zephyr/SKILL.md) and [`evaluate-zephyr-perf/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.agents/skills/evaluate-zephyr-perf/SKILL.md) — style/scope precedents (this skill is the missing third leg: pre-flight planner / post-mortem optimizer)

# Proposed approach (needs sign-off before writing the skill)

Split into two skills along the pre-job / post-job seam, since they use disjoint inputs and produce disjoint outputs:

**A. `plan-zephyr` (pre-job, no #5995 dep).** Input: a submission script or pipeline plan. Skill:
1. Resolves `InputFileSpec`s, enumerates files via fsspec, captures size and (for parquet) row counts.
2. Reports shard count and shard-size distribution (p50/p95/max/skew-ratio).
3. Picks `map_workers_per_actor`, `reduce_workers_per_actor`, and Iris `--memory` from a small heuristic table (e.g. memory = max(scatter-buffer-floor, p95 shard bytes × buffer-multiple); workers = min(cpu_count, p95-shard-mem-fit)).
4. Emits a diff against the user's submission command + a one-paragraph rationale. Does **not** auto-submit.

Doable now. ~100 LOC of skill prose + a small `scripts/zephyr/plan_inputs.py` helper for file enumeration (the heuristic itself stays in the skill prose; agents apply judgment).

**B. `tune-zephyr` (post-mortem, blocked on #5995).** Input: a finished or in-flight `iris_job_id`. Skill:
1. Pulls `zephyr.stage` rows for the run; flags stages where `item_rate` collapsed late (straggler signature) or `peak_worker_memory_mb` was close to allocation (under-provisioned).
2. Cross-references `iris.worker` (already exists) for OOM/preemption.
3. For skew, falls back to manual `actor call get_counters` per OPS.md until #5995 ships `zephyr.shard`.
4. Emits a recommended config delta for the next run, plus a "re-shard the input" recommendation when input skew is the dominant cost.

Out-of-scope for now (flag if you disagree):
- Auto-resubmitting with new params — risky without human review.
- Modifying scatter internals (covered by `evaluate-zephyr-perf`).
- CPU sizing — Iris already sets that per cluster config; not a Zephyr-side knob.

**Questions for @wmoss before I write either skill:**

- **(a) Split A/B or single skill?** I lean two skills (different inputs, different cadences, B blocks on #5995). Push back if you want one entry point.
- **(b) Output channel.** Print to terminal in the invoking chat (like `debug`), comment on a PR (like `evaluate-zephyr-perf`), or write a recommended config file? My default: terminal for A, comment on the issue/PR that owns the run for B.
- **(c) Heuristic provenance.** Do you have an existing rule-of-thumb for memory-per-shard / workers-per-actor I should encode, or should I derive defaults from a few representative ferries (datakit tier1/tier2/tier3) and bake those numbers in?
- **(d) Skew action.** When the skill flags skewed input shards, what's the recommended remediation in this codebase — a `repartition`/`reshuffle` op, manual `InputFileSpec` row-range splits, or just "tell the user and stop"?
- **(e) Defer B until #5995 lands?** Or stub it now against the proposed schema and update when #5995 lands?

Holding off on PRs pending answers, since (b)–(d) materially change the skill's content.

issues.author: wmoss
issues.body:
Parent issue for tracking work to get to a stable (version 1?) of Zephyr. This issue should be the home for everything required for the tactical burn down of Zephyr, as outlined in [State of the Infra -- May 2026](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tw-KevlFPRHQzXCDZeRfluPCk84QroJsn1zvHY8EzPE/edit?tab=t.0). The goal of this epic is also to provide a way to think bigger and longer term about Zephyr.

# Out of scope
Notably out of scope for this is providing a way to write sql to run distributed jobs over our infrastructure. We have discussed using [smallpond](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/smallpond) or attempting to push DuckDB deeper into Zephyr, but both of those are out of scope for this. Users will be able to use sql (using DataFusion or DuckDB) to process `RecordBatch` objects in mappers or reducers.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
The TPU Splash attention adapter ignores `AttentionMask.fa4_bounds`. A model that selects a per-layer local attention window through `with_fa4_bounds` runs every layer with full causal attention when `attention_implementation="tpu_splash"`. Nothing fails: the step traces and runs, and the output differs from the reference and GPU FA4 paths.

`_tpu_splash_attention` in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_core.py` builds its `SplashAttentionMaskSpec` from `mask.is_causal` and `mask.sliding_window` only. The models that vary the window per layer inside a `lax.scan` keep `sliding_window=None` on the long mask and pass the window as bounds, for example `layer_mask = long_mask.with_fa4_bounds(lower_bounds, valid)` in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py`, `moe_hero_fsdp/model.py`, `fast_track/model.py`, and the long-loop SFT runtime in PR 11120. The `fa4_bounds` field comment lists the FA4/CuTe kernel, the AMD Triton kernels and `materialize_mask` as consumers; Splash is not one of them.

Measured on CPU with the Splash Pallas interpreter, using a two-layer model (one local layer with a 128-token window, then one global layer), a 512-token packed sequence, context-parallel size 4, and byte-identical weights on both paths:

| Comparison | Max abs logit difference |
|---|---:|
| Splash vs reference attention | 6.36e-3 |
| Splash vs reference, window supplied to Splash as a static mask per layer | 1.49e-7 |
| Reference unrolled vs reference scan (control) | 0.0 |

This was found while bringing Snowball SFT up on a v4-128 slice. It may be related to the earlier observation that TPU-served Snowball output diverges from token 2048 onward, which is the local window size. That link is not established: this probe did not replay the serving code path.

Expected: either the Splash path honours the per-layer window, or it rejects a mask that carries `fa4_bounds` so the run fails at trace time.

Done when: a test compares Splash against reference attention on a mixed local/global layer schedule with a sequence longer than the window, and a mask with bounds can no longer reach Splash and be silently treated as full causal.

A candidate fix for the long-loop SFT model selects between two static Splash masks by the existing per-layer global flag; it matches the reference to 1.49e-7 on the probe above and will be proposed in a separate PR. A generic adapter cannot turn arbitrary per-query bounds into one static Splash window.

`_tpu_splash_attention` lowers only `is_causal` and `sliding_window`; `fa4_bounds` reaches it unchecked. The MoE layer scan selects the local window through those bounds while retaining `sliding_window=None`, so Splash runs a full causal mask for local layers. No open PR targets #11502 or this adapter behavior.

**Relevant code**

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The three CoreWeave clusters do not agree on ghcr credentials. Measured 2026-07-28 in namespace `iris`:

| cluster | `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` secret |
|---|---|
| cw-us-east-02a | `ghcr-helw150` |
| cw-rno2a | none |
| cw-us-east-08a | none |

`ghcr-helw150` was created 2026-07-02, holds one `ghcr.io` entry, and is referenced by no file under `lib/iris/config/`. It appears to be manual cluster state rather than anything the repo declares.

The effect is that a private or internal ghcr image runs on east-02a and fails on the other two with `ImagePullBackOff`. That asymmetry is hard to read from the symptom: the digest is valid, the image pulls fine from a laptop with `gh` credentials, and one cluster works. It looks like an image problem when it is a credential problem.

We hit this today. A rebuild moved our RL image from `ghcr.io/open-thoughts/openthoughts-agent` to a new package under `marin-community`. GitHub creates a new org package as internal by default. The old package was public, so cw-rno2a had never needed a pull secret and nothing recorded that it depended on that. Six RL jobs sat in `ImagePullBackOff` on cw-rno2a for about two and a half hours while the same digest ran normally on cw-us-east-02a. Setting the package public fixed it, and the pods recovered without intervention once kubelet's backoff came round.

Making every image public is a workaround, not a fix. It also means the clusters stay inconsistent for anything that genuinely cannot be public.

Reproduce:

```bash
for c in marin-gpu_US-EAST-02A marin-rn02a_RNO2A marin-us-east-08a_US-EAST-08A; do
  echo -n "$c: "
  kubectl --context $c -n iris get secrets \
    -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.type=="kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson")]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{end}'
  echo
done
```

Expected: the clusters carry the same ghcr credential, declared somewhere in `lib/iris/config/` rather than existing only in one live cluster, and named for the service rather than for an individual.

Worth deciding as part of that: whether task pods should be able to pull private images at all. If yes, all three clusters need the credential. If no, the constraint should be written down so nobody publishes an internal package and waits out a silent failure on two clusters.

Done when: pulling a private ghcr image behaves the same way on all three clusters, and the credential's existence is visible from the repo.

One note on verification, because it cost us time. An authenticated pull proves nothing here — your own credentials succeed against an internal package while a cluster node still cannot fetch it. Check anonymously:

```bash
DOCKER_CONFIG=$(mktemp -d) crane manifest --platform linux/amd64 <repository>@sha256:<digest>
```

cc @rjpower

comments.author: weaverbot
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

CoreWeave task configs leave `kubernetes_provider.service_account` empty, so `_build_pod_manifest()` omits `serviceAccountName` and Kubernetes assigns the mutable `default` ServiceAccount. A pull secret attached to that account changes registry access outside Iris config, which explains why the same private digest ran only on `cw-us-east-02a`.

**Relevant code**
- [`config.py#L625`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/config.py#L625) - task ServiceAccount setting
- [`composer.py#L125`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/composer.py#L125) - config enters backend
- [`tasks.py#L981`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L981) - optional Pod field
- [`rbac.py#L38`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/coreweave/rbac.py#L38) - IaC-owned accounts
- [`coreweave.md#L151`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/docs/coreweave.md#L151) - public-image contract

# Proposed Fix

Provision an unprivileged `iris-task` ServiceAccount with no `imagePullSecrets`, name it in every CoreWeave task config, and make controller startup reject a missing or credential-bearing task account. Document anonymous GHCR verification and remove the orphan `ghcr-helw150` credential from `cw-us-east-02a` as the one-time live cleanup.

comments.body: 🤖 PR #7722 declares an IaC-owned `iris-task` ServiceAccount with no pull credentials and selects it in all four persistent CoreWeave configs. All four Pulumi previews contain one ServiceAccount create and no destructive changes, but `cw-ci-test` now fails at the intended prerequisite check because `iris-ci/iris-task` is not live yet; this session has no CoreWeave kubeconfig. @rjpower, can you apply the `cw-us-west-04a` stack from this branch so CI can validate the rollout?

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 @rjpower, following up on your question above. We've since decided as an org *not* to make our baked image builds public, so "make the images public" no longer covers this case and we need a new solution.

The problem is live again. An internal `ghcr.io/marin-community` image (an RL environment image) couldn't be pulled on cw-rno2a: the pod got an anonymous GHCR 401 and went into `ImagePullBackOff`. To unblock that one job, there's a temporary manual pull secret on cw-rno2a (`iris/ghcr-read-pull`, a read-only `read:packages` token on the `default` service account). That's the same kind of undeclared, single-cluster state this issue was opened about, so it shouldn't be the long-term answer. #7722 (a credential-free task service account) was closed unmerged, and #9996 (envreg pulls for sandbox pods) is still open.

We need a supported way for Iris tasks on every CoreWeave cluster to pull private org images, owned by a service identity and declared in IaC. Is #9996's envreg route the intended path, or should we reopen this?

## Decision: version the Skill2Env source with only permissively licensed tasks

**User decision (2026-11-16 ~08:45 EST), verbatim:** “drop the tasks with non-standard licenses, version the source, document the decision in gh issue”.

### Source

`open-athena/harbor-hub-skill2env-d208e05b-taskcompendium-20261112` @ `6198459210ab98e0c9c4e021b20f50e93c41b9d4` — 7,496 native Harbor tasks converted from the Harbor Hub release `skill2env/skill2env@sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`, which NVIDIA generated from [NVlabs/Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) (project Apache-2.0; per-skill third-party grants inventoried in `SkillHub/skillhub_source_licenses.csv`).

This source has been banned as "Applicable permissive origin grant and exact release lineage have not been established." ([#11497](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11497)).

### Mapping (provenance, not guessed IDs)

Each native task package's `task.toml` carries `source_skill` (the SkillHub skill path) and `source_bundle_digest`. All 7,496 packages' provenance was read from the pinned input archives, then joined against `SkillHub/skillhub_source_licenses.csv` at the pinned origin commit `NVlabs/Skill2Env@a99ad513b438021ed384c60b0a6bdf650afe0a2a` (2,396 skill rows; every component of each AND-listed license checked against the accepted permissive list).

### Counts

| Outcome | Tasks |
|---|---:|
| Retained (skill license accepted: MIT 2,461; Apache-2.0 556; MIT AND Apache-2.0 106; Apache-2.0 AND CC-BY-4.0 38; MIT AND CC-BY-4.0 and Apache-2.0 AND MIT 2) | **6,159** |
| Dropped — non-standard upstream skill license | **3** |
| Dropped — skill license unestablished at the pinned origin (1,315 skills absent from the CSV; 19 tasks with ambiguous identity) | **1,334** |

Dropped non-standard licenses, quoted: `Apache-2.0 AND OFL-1.1` (anthropic/canvas-design, https://github.com/anthropics/skills) and `MIT AND Apache-2.0 AND ISC AND BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND CC0-1.0 AND Zlib AND EPL-2.0 AND EPL-1.0 AND Apache-1.1` (garry-tan/gstack, https://github.com/garrytan/gstack).

### New version

Published as a **private** dataset: [`open-athena/harbor-hub-skill2env-d208e05b-license-filtered-20261116-v1` @ `d9d97af0b8d75c5132a71c194ced9af75f0309ae`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/harbor-hub-skill2env-d208e05b-license-filtered-20261116-v1/tree/d9d97af0b8d75c5132a71c194ced9af75f0309ae), carrying the filtered `tasks.parquet`, the per-task license manifest, and the dropped task references with reasons. Retained task specs are byte-identical to the pinned source. The card declares the checked origin (`license_source` → NVlabs/Skill2Env at the pinned commit); the deterministic license checker returns **PASS P1** at this pin.

The old pin stays banned; the ban does not apply to the new source identity. The new version goes through the normal pipeline (census, decontamination, oracle/NoP, SAMPLE, admission) like any other source.

Labelled `agent-generated` per repository policy.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Summary

Snowball (67B MoE) long-loop SFT now trains on TPU v4. A 20-update run on a v4-128 slice (64 chips) finished on 2026-11-15 with finite losses and a written checkpoint. This issue records what works, what was fixed, and what is still unproven, so others can use the TPU cluster for SFT.

## Result

Setup: long-loop SFT recipe from the 10/05 Snowball checkpoint, 16 hosts x 4 chips (v4-128), small test batch of 131,072 token positions per update.

| Run | Updates | Outcome |
|---|---:|---|
| Fit proxy (all layers global attention) | 1 | Succeeded, 8.99 chip-hours |
| Real recipe with window fix | 1 | Succeeded, 9.14 chip-hours |
| Real recipe with window fix | 20 | Succeeded, 15.04 chip-hours |

Measured on the 20-update run:

- 7.70 s per update in steady state, 17,029 token positions per second (266 per chip).
- End to end 847 s, including compile (about 33-36 s) and checkpoint write.
- Checkpoint: 801 GB in 584 objects; write and drain took 191 s.
- 20 finite loss rows; all 16 hosts succeeded.

## Fixes needed to get there

- **Segment IDs were sharded differently from the query inputs** under context parallelism, which failed at trace time (`Invalid shape for q segment_ids: (8192,). Expected: (2048,)`). Fix: PR 11506 (draft).
- **TPU Splash attention ignored the per-layer local window**, so local layers ran full causal attention. A 2-layer CPU probe showed a max logit difference of 6.4e-3 against the reference, and 1.5e-7 after the fix. Tracked in issue 11502; fix for the long-loop branch in PR 11507 (draft). The same pattern exists in other model files on main.
- **`mixture_block_size` must divide the stage start index.** The data config value is sized for batch 256; a small batch needs a smaller block.

## Limits

- **Not a matched speed comparison.** Three unrelated 64-H100 SFT arms measured 1,044-2,907 positions per second per H100, against 266 per v4 chip here. The TPU run used a small untuned batch, and nothing was measured per dollar.
- **Only v4-128 was tried.** Scaling to v4-512 or larger is not measured.
- **No TPU-trained checkpoint has been evaluated.** Equal quality to an H100-trained checkpoint is not shown.
- The per-host sharding dump and actual dtypes were not captured in the first runs.

## Next steps

- [ ] One run of at most 1 hour on the largest available v4 slice with the full recipe batch; report positions per second in total and per chip.
- [ ] One matched SFT arm on TPU and on H100, scored on the same evals.
- [ ] Land PR 11506 and PR 11507; close issue 11502 for the remaining model files.
- [ ] If both hold, document the TPU SFT launch path next to the long-loop recipe.

The long-loop runtime is in #11120; #11505, #11506, and #11507 cover the attention prerequisites. #11293 overlaps #11506 on packed Splash metadata, so those drafts need one reconciled source revision before the next run.

Plan:
1. Pin the source revision, 10/05 checkpoint, run spec, data manifests, and evaluation inputs. Validate context-parallel packed attention and the mixed local/global window against the reference, check `mixture_block_size` against the full-batch stage start, and capture per-host sharding and actual dtypes.
2. Use the largest available v4 slice for one full-recipe-batch run capped at one hour. Record slice size, finite-loss updates, scheduled positions, steady update time, total and per-chip positions/s, chip-hours, checkpoint size/write time, and cost per million positions if billing data is available. Compare scaling with the 64-chip v4-128 baseline here, separating compile and checkpoint time from steady training.
3. Train TPU and H100 SFT arms from the same 10/05 checkpoint with pinned data order, packing, token budget, effective batch, and optimizer schedule. Score the resulting checkpoints with the same pinned evaluation and decoding settings; report per-benchmark scores, sample counts, uncertainty, training cost, and any hardware-dependent configuration differences. comments.body:
🤖 **PARTIAL result: Snowball TPU SFT on one v4-256 slice (128 chips), 20 updates.** The per-rank artifacts are not yet reviewed (listed at the end).

**Setup.** v4-256 = 32 hosts × 4 chips, one slice in us-central2-b, production priority, no retries. Changes from the earlier v4-128 run (64 chips, batch 16 × 8,192, accumulation 1, which ran clean): batch **256 × 8,192** (the recipe's 256 sequences, at 8k context), gradient accumulation 8 (still one sequence per data replica per microbatch), and the recipe's mixture block of 64,000. Unchanged from that run: model, base checkpoint, ring MoE, MuonH, the configured FP32 stored parameters with BF16 compute, and context axis 4. Configured mesh: data 32 × context 4, one slice, no DCN axis. The actual per-rank dtypes and sharding are not yet read.

**Observed:**

| | |
|---|---|
| Tasks | 32/32 succeeded on the first attempt; no retry, no preemption of our job |
| Losses | all 20 finite: 0.833 at update 1, 0.657–0.764 over updates 11–20 (different minibatches under warmup, so not a convergence claim) |
| Steady step time, updates 4–20 | **67.6 s** (range 67.46–68.07 s), rank-0 logged duration |
| Throughput | **31,021 positions/s** total, **242 per chip**. This is a nominal position rate, 2,097,152 positions over the rank-0 logged duration; all-rank timing is still pending. The v4-128 run gave 266 per chip at batch 16 without accumulation. The chip count, batch and accumulation all changed together, so this is not a scaling law. |
| First update | logged duration 120.6 s (includes the first-step compile). Placement to the start of update 1 was about 7.8 min, and placement to its logged completion (15:51:13Z) about 9.8 min. |
| Checkpoint at update 20 | 801.07 GB in 760 objects (storage listing). All 32 hosts started saving in the same second and logged the commit barrier complete about 95 s later (log timestamps). The v4-128 run took 191 s with 16 writers. This shows the writes and the barrier, not restore or full tensor integrity. |
| Cost | **70.62 chip-hours**; 33 min end to end |

**Not yet reviewed:** the 32 per-rank timing journals (the all-rank compute range and the drain spans), the 64 compiled-memory reports, the 32 per-rank dtype/sharding reports, and the contents of the checkpoint metadata and manifest. The files exist; reading and checking them is pending. The numbers above come from task records, rank-0 metric logs, log timestamps and storage listings.

**Not established:** checkpoint restore, model quality, 32k context, or equivalence with the H100 recipe (which runs 32,768-token sequences, so 4× more positions per update).

**Next, an estimate:** a real 150-update C-recipe arm on v4-256 needs three things: the C config in the TPU entry point (its MuonH grouping, the 10/05 base in us-central2, the C mixture); 32k context qualified on TPU; and either checkpoint restore qualified or the whole run fitting in one job. Arithmetic only: **if** the measured 8k rate of 31,021 positions/s held at 32k (untested), one full-size update of 8.39M positions would take about 270 s, and 150 updates about 11.25 h of compute, plus startup and checkpoints. This is not an expected 32k runtime: throughput and memory at 32k context are not qualified.

issues.author: asartran
issues.body:
Two taskforge test modules import shared test helpers through the top-level name `tests`, which only resolves to `lib/taskforge/tests` when pytest runs with taskforge's own config. When the nightly CI `slow` job collects every package from the repo root, `tests` resolves to Marin's top-level `tests/` package and collection fails:

```
ERROR lib/taskforge/tests/llm/test_rollout_model.py
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'ListLedger' from 'tests.conftest' (/home/runner/work/marin/marin/tests/conftest.py)
ERROR lib/taskforge/tests/spec/test_draft.py
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests.sandbox'
```

The imports are at `lib/taskforge/tests/llm/test_rollout_model.py:54-55` (`from tests.conftest import ListLedger`, `from tests.sandbox.fixture_images import ...`) and `lib/taskforge/tests/spec/test_draft.py:84`. They arrived with the taskforge stack (#10293-#10296) on Nov 2, and the nightly slow job has failed on them every night since Nov 3. The `taskforge-unit` job passes because it runs `pytest -c lib/taskforge/pyproject.toml`, so `--import-mode=importlib` names modules relative to `lib/taskforge`.

#11426 makes the nightly slow job skip `lib/taskforge/tests` as a stopgap; taskforge has no slow-marked tests, so no coverage is lost today, but any slow test added to taskforge would not run nightly.

Done when:
- `lib/taskforge/tests` collects without errors from the repo root with the root pytest config, for example `uv run --all-packages --group test pytest --collect-only lib/taskforge/tests`;
- the nightly slow job in `.github/workflows/unified-unit.yaml` no longer leaves `lib/taskforge/tests` out of its test paths.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Root-level pytest collection imports the top-level `tests` package, so Taskforge's `from tests.*` imports resolve to Marin's test tree. Taskforge's own pytest configuration gives those modules a different import root, which hides the collision.

**Relevant code**
- [`test_rollout_model.py#L54-L55`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskforge/tests/llm/test_rollout_model.py#L54-L55) — shared helper imports
- [`test_draft.py#L84`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskforge/tests/spec/test_draft.py#L84) — sandbox fixture import
- [`unified-unit.yaml#L143-L153`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/unified-unit.yaml#L143-L153) — repo-root nightly collection

# Proposed Fix

Use relative imports from the Taskforge test modules to their shared helpers, then verify collection with both the root and Taskforge pytest configurations. The temporary skip is still only in open PR #11426; current `main` has no skip to remove.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 PR #11427 fixes the root-level import collision. All 418 Taskforge tests collect with the root pytest config; the 71 tests in the changed modules pass with Taskforge’s config. The taskforge-unit and marin-lint CI checks pass. The temporary skip remains only in #11426, whose author has been asked to close it after #11427 lands.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Fix Pi timeout and cancellation handling in Marin's vendored Harbor runtime. Stop Pi and its child processes before verification starts, so verifier commands can run in the same Daytona session without waiting for leftover agent work.

The [Harbor investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/261) includes a no-model reproduction of this mechanism. A [two-task Luna BixBench smoke](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/261#issuecomment-6372492452) reached the 1,800-second agent limit and then the 300-second verifier limit on both tasks, leaving both ungraded. [Saved Ben and Will evaluation attempts](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/261#issuecomment-6372692406) show the same timing pattern across Pi 1.3.0 and 1.4.0. Historical live process state was not captured, so the mechanism is not proven for every failed attempt.

Ben previously diagnosed remote commands surviving cancellation in [Harbor #13](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/13). The merged [OpenCode fix, #40](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/40), added a remote deadline and OpenCode-specific cleanup. That cleanup does not terminate Pi.

The fix belongs in Marin's vendored runtime: `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py` and, if needed, `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/daytona/environment.py`. Scope this issue to Pi on Daytona; a redesign of cancellation across all agents and providers is separate work.

Done when:

- Pi and its child processes stop on agent timeout or cancellation before verification begins; the persistent Daytona session remains usable.
- Regression coverage exercises timeout, explicit cancellation, and ordinary completion, including a child process that would otherwise write after the deadline.
- A bounded live Daytona probe exercises the vendored Pi execution path using a no-model test executable that spawns a child process. Trigger timeout and explicit cancellation through Harbor, without directly killing the test processes. Verify that neither process survives or writes afterward and that a verifier command completes in the same session. Preserve the logs and clean up the sandbox; no model or judge calls are required.
- Timeout classification and grading behavior remain consistent with Harbor's agent-timeout handling; benchmark time budgets are unchanged.

Evaluation adoption should use a merged Marin revision recorded in the run provenance. Historical results remain unchanged.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`Trial._await_phase()` cancels Pi's local task at the agent deadline, but Daytona submits its shell with `run_async=True`, so cancelling the poll does not stop the remote command. Pi launches `pi | node | tee` without a remote deadline, and Daytona's cancellation cleanup targets only `opencode`. This is consistent with the [no-model Harbor reproduction](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/261); the historical failed runs did not capture live process state.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial.py#L515-L594`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3bf0d7a1beaae9351f194ea41eb8f44a9421e945/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/trial.py#L515-L594) — agent deadline and cancellation.
- [`pi.py#L658-L699`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3bf0d7a1beaae9351f194ea41eb8f44a9421e945/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L658-L699) — Pi pipeline without remote deadline.
- [`environment.py#L1941-L2027`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3bf0d7a1beaae9351f194ea41eb8f44a9421e945/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/daytona/environment.py#L1941-L2027) — detached exec and OpenCode-only reap.
- [`trial.py#L715-L741`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3bf0d7a1beaae9351f194ea41eb8f44a9421e945/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/trial.py#L715-L741) — verifier uses the same environment.

# Proposed Fix

1. Isolate each Pi run in a uniquely identified remote process group. Apply a Daytona-side deadline from `environment.agent_timeout_sec` with bounded TERM and KILL of the group and its children; classify a deadline exit as `AgentTimeoutError` without changing the configured agent or verifier budgets.
2. On explicit cancellation or local timeout, terminate that exact Pi process tree through a separate, bounded Daytona control session. Cover cancellation during command submission as well as polling. Wait for confirmed exit before verification; if cleanup cannot be confirmed, fail the trial and retain diagnostics instead of grading alongside a live agent.
3. Add behavior tests in `test_pi.py` with a no-model executable that spawns a delayed-writing child. Cover normal completion, timeout, and explicit cancellation; add Daytona session tests for cleanup and the verifier's ability to execute afterward.
4. Run a bounded live Daytona probe through Harbor's vendored Pi path. Trigger timeout and cancellation, check that neither Pi nor its child survives or writes after the deadline, run a verifier command in the same session, save logs, and delete the sandbox. Daytona credentials are absent from this session, so this gate needs a credentialed runner.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Implementing this in Marin; the PR will remain draft. The current working change gives each Pi invocation a unique supervisor/control directory and uses a separate Daytona session for cancellation. Pi can launch tools in detached process groups, so the supervisor walks and stops the descendant process tree, including a detached child that ignores TERM, before killing it.

The Pi and Daytona test files currently pass (183 tests). New behavior coverage runs the vendored Pi/Daytona execution path against a local SDK-boundary fake with real subprocesses and a per-session queue: deadline, explicit cancellation during polling, normal completion, and subsequent verifier execution.

Your submission-cancellation and cleanup-failure requirements are still being addressed. In particular, `Trial._await_phase()` currently converts exceptions raised during timeout cleanup into the original `AgentTimeoutError`; a failed remote cleanup must remain a fatal infrastructure error so verification cannot proceed. The bounded live Daytona probe is also pending. No evaluation rerun has been launched.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Addressed in draft PR #10612. Cancellation during submission and polling now runs scoped cleanup in a separate Daytona session. If cleanup fails or cannot be confirmed within its bound, `PhaseCancellationError` remains fatal and verification does not proceed.

The final targeted suite passes 203 tests; the full Harbor offline runner passes 1,046 tests after rebasing onto main. A live no-model probe through vendored `Pi.run` and Daytona's session path passed all three cases: remote deadline (`AgentTimeoutError`, 5.28 seconds), explicit cancellation (`CancelledError`, 2.46 seconds), and normal completion (1.44 seconds). The timeout/cancellation cases checked Pi and a detached, TERM-ignoring child were gone or exited, with no delayed output; all cases then ran `verifier-ready` in the same session. The probe used a fake Pi executable and mapped the log file to a writable temporary path. Sandbox deletion was verified.

The supervisor stops parents before enumerating and killing descendants, since Pi tools can create their own process groups. This uses Linux `/proc`; it is not containment for processes that deliberately reparent themselves. No model calls or benchmark reruns were made. The PR remains draft.

issues.body:
Native SFTSpec Snowball d1024 training on one 8×H100 node passes forward evaluation but can hang in the first optimizer update. Every GPU reports 100% utilization, zero memory traffic and roughly 120–215W; Python rank main threads remain in XLA ExecuteReplicated. No completed update appears after more than five minutes. This blocks unmodified-runtime loss curves and throughput comparisons. d768 full-target training also stalled; d768 assistant-target and both d512 masks completed 20 updates.

Reproduce:
1. Load `open-athena/Snowflake-d1024-Base-262K-2026.10.19` at revision `dd3c5e3c156cfbe936fc0b59932c747e47c21d04` through native SFTSpec→TrainLmConfig→train_lm. Use sequence length 262144, global batch 8, microbatch 1, context parallel 4/data parallel 2, expert parallel 1, FP32 master parameters, BF16 computation, Sonic dispatch, gpu_fa4_cute attention, offloaded Muon-H optimizer and cuda_async allocator. The raw HF checkpoint evaluation and a second evaluation after resetting seven output-head token columns to fixed anchor columns both finish and match independently computed losses within 0.001. Training controls use assistant-only targets, data/trainer seed 0, sequential 262144-position packing and the pinned phase 0 Experiment 1 mixture. Its complete component paths, weights, reserved split and shuffle settings are in the consumed-config receipt linked below.
2. Use `XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false --xla_gpu_nccl_termination_timeout_seconds=600"` and execute the first backward/update. The local reproduction entry point is `experiments/post_training/snowball_isoflop/diagnostic.py`; source 33b69d10df preserves the isolated controls and later 97f6a242e6 exposes the explicit SFTSpec runtime field. These commits are local research commits, currently unpublished.
3. Compare the controls below, each starting from the same two-flag baseline in step 2. Baseline command-buffer and async-collective behavior is left at the JAX runtime default; neither has an extra override. Read-only inspection of a fresh campaign worker confirms jax, jaxlib, jax-cuda13-plugin and jax-cuda13-pjrt all 0.11.1. These match the GPU dependency pins used by the diagnostic source.

Expected: the first optimizer update completes, followed by finite training steps, without forced host launch synchronization.

| Runtime control | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Source async-collective runtime | First-update stall |
| Add `--xla_gpu_disable_async_collectives=ALLCOLLECTIVES` | First-update stall; NCCL collective counts agree across all ranks (AllGather 1460, ReduceScatter 99, AllReduce 46 globally) |
| Add only `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | First-update stall |
| Add only `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=` | First-update stall |
| Both command buffers off and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | 20 finite updates, permanent step 19 checkpoint, both initial-loss gates pass |
| Source runtime under Nsight Systems CUDA/NVTX tracing | 14 finite updates before deliberate bounded termination; CUDA graphs remain active |

The successful unprofiled joint control's first update took about 99 seconds; subsequent warm inclusive median 9.2473s/update, minimum unused allocator capacity 55.54% (the JAX allocator is limited to approximately 75% of physical GPU memory). One profiled run progressed while the unprofiled source-runtime attempt stalled; repeatability of this difference is not established. Its available trace contains 1,531,280 kernels across all 8 GPUs and 91,112 cuGraphLaunch calls. The report emitted a StringStorage processing warning, so exported events have that caveat. Successful completed kernels do not identify the operation stuck in unprofiled execution. NCCL 2.31.2, CUDA runtime 13.3, driver API 13.2 were reported. Agreement of NCCL counters in the synchronous-collective control does not prove which kernel or communication operation is responsible.

Preserved profile: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/snowball-isoflop/2026.11.13.9/diagnostic-kernel-profile-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20/nsys/r00000-gb95de0.nsys-rep` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fsnowball-isoflop%2F2026.11.13.9%2Fdiagnostic-kernel-profile-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20%2Fnsys%2Fr00000-gb95de0.nsys-rep)); exported summary is `analysis/kernel-summary.json` beside its nsys directory. The complete successful joint-control config is [available in Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fsnowball-isoflop%2F2026.11.13.9%2Fdiagnostic-synchronous-launches-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20%2Fconsumed-config.json). Related investigations: #7110 (concurrent TVM-FFI invocation), #8870 (multi-rack ragged EP hang). This single-node CP4/data2 Sonic case has not been reduced to either mechanism.

Fresh six-cell calibration update (2026-11-14 02:51UTC): both d1024 masks with the joint runtime progressed beyond15 finite updates. All source-runtime failed-arm receipts remain under `2026.11.13.10/calibration-d{512,768}-{full,assistant}-seed0-n20/`; their scoped recovery uses separate `calibration-recovery-` identities.

Adding `--xla_gpu_disable_async_collectives=ALLCOLLECTIVES` to that joint setting completed20 finite updates for BOTH d512 masks and BOTH d768 masks, with dual initial-loss gates, finished trackers, permanent step19 checkpoints and safe allocator headroom. The corresponding SFTSpec runtime implementation is in local research source3a38e030d0 (unpublished).

A source-runtime d1024 `ring_gather_combine` control at CP4/data2 also stalled at the first update. A late CUDA-GDB attachment timed out before kernel queries; the job later failed, so retain an intervention caveat and do not infer a particular blocked kernel. Its archived output is preserved at `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/snowball-isoflop/2026.11.13.10/diagnostic-ring-r2/debugger-outputs.tar.zst` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fsnowball-isoflop%2F2026.11.13.10%2Fdiagnostic-ring-r2%2Fdebugger-outputs.tar.zst)).

Minimum allocator headroom80.19%; warm inclusive71,600 positions/s/GPU. Its supervisor recorded a rank0 cleanup segfault, although job, tracker and native checkpoint gates passed. All compared layout diagnostics use dispatch-count instrumentation, which differs from the main calibration and remains an attribution caveat. CP4/data2 offload-false was interrupted before training, so it does not establish an offload result. Geometry is a useful discriminator; a causal kernel mechanism remains unproven.

Batch-probe update (2026-11-14 04:35UTC): original SOURCE runtime also stalls d512, d768 and d1024 assistant-target CP4/data2/Sonic/offload-true probes at global batch2, microbatch1, accumulation1. All three pass both initial gates; none records an update more than9 minutes after the first batch is loaded. Read-only snapshots show all24GPUs at100% utilization and0% memory utilization, approximately118–217W. d512/d1024 main threads remain in ExecuteReplicated; d768 waits on ArrayImpl._value while reading the resulting loss scalar. Each stalled probe was stopped; total allocation6.64272H100-hours. These cells provide no valid throughput or batch-saturation measurements. Exact receipts are under `2026.11.13.10/B-accumulation-cp4-dp2-ep1-r1-sonic-offload1-mb1-acc1-grug_moe_muonh_v1-lr5e-05-d{512,768,1024}-assistant-seed0-n8/` beside the previous artifacts. This extends the observed failure beyond accumulation4/globalbatch8, without proving its cause.

The d1024 full-mask three-setting runtime (joint setting plus ALLCOLLECTIVES) also completed20 finite updates, both initial gates, finished tracking and a permanent step19 checkpoint. The matching assistant confirmation is running; uniform loss-phase runtime has not yet been selected from that pending result.

CP8 feasibility update (2026-11-14 04:59UTC): source-runtime batch8/microbatch1/accumulation8/Sonic/offload-true probes completed8 finite updates for d512 AND d768. Both have finished trackers, dual initial-loss gates, permanent step7 checkpoints and zero measured sender/receiver drops. Warm inclusive positions/s/GPU are48,324 and48,514; minimum allocator headroom81.20% and73.08%. Both supervisors killed rank0 during cleanup despite successful job/tracker/checkpoint gates. The d1024 CP8 cell passed both initial gates but stalled before its first update; two read-only samples several minutes apart show ExecuteReplicated and all8GPUs100% utilization/0% memory utilization/~118–130W. It was stopped after both smaller endpoints were verified. Thus CP8 is a positive discriminator for two sizes, not a universal recovery. The three-setting d1024 assistant confirmation also completed its first update and reached final native checkpoint/export, but its3-H100-hour bound interrupted export with only19 published training rows. comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The compiled training step computes gradients and applies the optimizer in one execution. The reported forward evaluations and runtime controls do not identify which operation stalls. Command buffers disabled together with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` completed 20 updates; each control alone stalled. One source-runtime run under Nsight reached 14 updates, but repeatability is unknown. The cited diagnostic commits `33b69d10df` and `97f6a242e6` are absent from this checkout and GitHub; the exact workload cannot yet be reproduced from published source. [#7110](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7110) and [#8870](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8870) involve different kernels or topologies and do not identify this stall.

**Relevant code**
- [`trainer.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L726-L749) — gradients and optimizer share a compiled step.
- [`snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L430-L455) — Snowball attention dispatch.
- [`_fa4_cute.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute.py#L311-L335) — H100 attention backend.
- [`sonic.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/sonic.py#L248-L310) — Sonic dispatch and backward.
- [`muonh.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/optim/muonh.py#L54-L100) — Muon-H optimizer construction.

# Proposed Fix

1. Publish the isolated `diagnostic.py`, its SFTSpec runtime field, and exact dependency pins in a reviewable branch. Link its consumed-config receipt. Give every trial a first-update deadline and preserve its result and source revision.
2. On the same 8×H100 configuration, repeat the source runtime and passing joint control three times each. Run a separate traced source-runtime arm to measure the Nsight effect. Record per-rank progress, NCCL RAS, XLA executable dumps, and loaded CUDA/NCCL versions; stop each stalled trial after a 10-minute first-update deadline.
3. Split the first update at the gradient/optimizer boundary with the same parameters, batch, and mesh: evaluate gradients without applying them, then apply the optimizer to captured gradients. If gradients stall, replace FA4 and Sonic independently. Capture a GPU kernel/stream stack from a stalled rank before changing more runtime flags. These ablations localize a suspect; they do not by themselves prove a cause if recompilation changes launch order.
4. Fix the identified component in Marin or report a minimal reproducer upstream. Validate the original unprofiled runtime without launch synchronization across three cold 20-update runs, with finite losses, the existing initial-loss gates, and warm-step timing against the 9.2473 s joint-control median. Add a regression test for the isolated failure before opening a fix PR.

[Width-512 repeat 1](https://iris-cw-rno2a.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fsnowball-11440-no-autotune-r2) · [Width-512 repeat 2](https://iris-cw-rno2a.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fsnowball-11440-no-autotune-r3) · [Width-1024](https://iris-cw-rno2a.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fsnowball-11440-d1024-no-autotune)

issues.author: asonnino
issues.body:
**Summary.** After the last training step, `Trainer.train()` calls the checkpoint hook with `force=True`, and `Checkpointer.on_step(force=True)` saves that step again even when it was already saved, into the same `step-N/` directory, while the `metadata.json` from the first save (the commit marker) stays in place. On a local file system, a crash after the re-save has opened `manifest.json` for writing can leave `step-N/` looking committed but with an empty manifest, so every restart picks it and fails until an operator deletes it. We did not test object stores, where an object is replaced only when its write completes. The smallest fix we see is to write `manifest.json` through `atomic_rename`, as `_save_metadata` already does for `metadata.json` (see "Suggested fix"); we can open a PR for it. ## Affected versions - Reproduced on 2026-11-13 with the standalone script below on marin-levanter 0.2.274.dev43433851997 and 0.2.268.dev43309064464, and on marin `main` at [`a922ffc`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/a922ffc740488a3aa82c8ac3f8cf8e9dd8d77ba7) (its `levanter` package installed over the 0.2.274 wheel, which it matches file for file), TensorStore 0.1.84, JAX 0.12.0.1 on CPU, local file system. It also reproduced on 2026-11-10 on 0.2.260.dev42827925033 and on `main` at `2b3b0a04`. - The links below pin `4aab2cff`. At `a922ffc`, `checkpoint.py`, `tensorstore_serialization.py` and `checkpoint_manifest.py` are unchanged, and the linked lines of `trainer.py` are two lines further down with the same content. ## Impact - **Loud**: every restart fails with `ValidationError: 1 validation error for CheckpointManifest ... Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0 [type=json_invalid, input_value='', input_type=str]`. - **Needs an operator** to delete `step-N/` (or its `metadata.json`). If `step-N` was the run's first permanent checkpoint (the `--permanent` case below), no loadable checkpoint is left and the run then restarts from scratch; otherwise the previous permanent checkpoint remains. - **No operator action** is needed to trigger it, whenever the last step was already saved before the forced save: - the last step is a multiple of a `keep` `every` interval (a permanent save). The forced save is permanent too and goes to the same `step-N/` under `base_path`, so this holds whether or not `temporary_base_path` is set; - the `save_interval` timer fires on the last step (a temporary save), with `temporary_base_path` unset (the default); - from the code (not tested): a completed run is restarted, since `train()` then runs the forced hooks for the step it loaded ([trainer.py#L618-L625](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L618-L625)). [#9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) reports this re-save on a resume from the final step, where it fails for another reason. - The window is short: from opening `manifest.json`, one small JSON file, to the end of its write. We injected crashes only into this file of the re-save; the array data of the re-save goes into the same OCDBT database and was not tested. ## Reproduction Standalone script (single process, JAX on CPU), in the collapsible block below. It drives `Checkpointer` the way `Trainer.train()` does and kills the process right after the forced re-save opens `step-N/manifest.json` for writing.
levanter_final_resave.py ```python """Levanter: a crash during the end-of-training re-save of an already-saved step leaves it unloadable. python levanter_final_resave.py [--permanent] Run 1 saves steps 1 to 3 (step 2 permanent because every=2, steps 1 and 3 temporary because save_interval has elapsed), then makes the forced save that Trainer.train() makes after its last step (Checkpointer.on_step(force=True)) into the same step-3/ directory, and is killed right after that save opens step-3/manifest.json for writing. With --permanent, run 1 stops at step 2, so the forced save rewrites the permanent step-2/. Run 2 discovers the latest checkpoint and loads it. """ import builtins import datetime import os import subprocess import sys import tempfile import time import jax.numpy as jnp from levanter.checkpoint import Checkpointer, CheckpointInterval, latest_checkpoint_path, load_checkpoint STATE = {"model": jnp.arange(4.0)} LAST = 2 if "--permanent" in sys.argv else 3 def checkpointer(base): return Checkpointer(base, save_interval=datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=1), step_policies=[CheckpointInterval(every=2)]) if __name__ == "__main__": if sys.argv[1:2] == ["crash"]: ckpt = checkpointer(sys.argv[2]) for step in range(1, LAST + 1): time.sleep(0.01) ckpt.on_step(tree=STATE, step=step) ckpt.wait_until_finished() real_open = builtins.open def crashing_open(file, mode="r", *args, **kwargs): f = real_open(file, mode, *args, **kwargs) if str(file).endswith(f"step-{LAST}/manifest.json") and "w" in mode: os._exit(137) # the file has just been opened for writing, so it is now empty return f builtins.open = crashing_open ckpt.on_step(tree=STATE, step=LAST, force=True) # what Trainer.train() does after the last step sys.exit("not killed") base = tempfile.mkdtemp() rc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, __file__, "crash", base] + sys.argv[1:]).returncode print(f"run 1 killed (exit {rc}); checkpoints: {sorted(os.listdir(base))}; step-{LAST}/: " f"{sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(base, f'step-{LAST}')))}", flush=True) path = latest_checkpoint_path(base) print(f"latest checkpoint: {os.path.basename(path)}", flush=True) try: load_checkpoint(STATE, path) print("loaded") except Exception as e: print(f"load failed: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:300]}") ```
Output on 0.2.274.dev43433851997 (the same on 0.2.268.dev43309064464 and on marin `main` at `a922ffc`; pydantic's help link removed): ```text $ python levanter_final_resave.py run 1 killed (exit 137); checkpoints: ['step-2', 'step-3']; step-3/: ['d', 'manifest.json', 'manifest.ocdbt', 'metadata.json'] latest checkpoint: step-3 load failed: ValidationError: 1 validation error for CheckpointManifest Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0 [type=json_invalid, input_value='', input_type=str] $ python levanter_final_resave.py --permanent run 1 killed (exit 137); checkpoints: ['step-2']; step-2/: ['d', 'manifest.json', 'manifest.ocdbt', 'metadata.json'] latest checkpoint: step-2 load failed: ValidationError: 1 validation error for CheckpointManifest Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0 [type=json_invalid, input_value='', input_type=str] ``` In the second case no loadable checkpoint is left. ## Expected vs actual - Expected: the final step that was already committed stays loadable; at most its `is_temporary` flag changes. - Actual: the committed `step-N/` is rewritten in place under its old `metadata.json`, and a crash during the rewrite makes it unloadable while discovery still selects it. ## Root cause 1. [`train()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L627-L638) runs the hooks once more with `force=True` after the loop, for the same step whose regular hooks already ran inside [`train_step`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L571); the [checkpoint hook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L656-L662) passes `force` to `Checkpointer.on_step`. 2. [`on_step`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L605-L607) skips an already saved step only when `force` is false, and the forced save always uses [`destination = f"step-{step}"`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L644-L670) under `base_path`, which is the directory of the first save when that save was permanent or `temporary_base_path` is unset. `save_checkpoint` reuses it ([`fs.makedirs(plain_path, exist_ok=True)`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L866)). 3. Process 0 then rewrites `manifest.json` in place ([tensorstore_serialization.py#L645-L648](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tensorstore_serialization.py#L645-L648), [`write_manifest`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint_manifest.py#L64-L65), a plain `StoragePath.write_text`, which on a local path truncates the file when it opens it), while the old `metadata.json` remains. Discovery treats any directory with a `metadata.json` as complete ([checkpoint.py#L1245-L1246](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L1245-L1246)), so it selects the half-rewritten step. [`_save_metadata`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L931-L947), by contrast, writes `metadata.json` through `atomic_rename` on local paths. [`Checkpointer.save_final_checkpoint`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L752-L757) already skips a step whose last save was permanent, but `Trainer.train()` does not call it (its callers are `tests/test_checkpoint.py` and five grug training scripts), and it still re-saves a temporary step into the same directory. ## Suggested fix From the smallest: 1. Write `manifest.json` through `atomic_rename` on local paths, as `_save_metadata` does for `metadata.json`. With this change as a monkeypatch on 0.2.268, and the kill moved to the opening of the temporary file, both modes of the script load the checkpoint after the crash, and a `manifest.json.tmp.` file is left next to `manifest.json`. It does not change when a re-save happens. The array data of the re-save, which goes into the same OCDBT database, was not tested. 2. Or, on local paths, uncommit first (remote permanent prefixes can deny deletes, as PR [#9215](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9215) describes): remove `metadata.json` before saving into a committed directory and write it back once the manifest and data are complete, so that a crash leaves the step ignored by discovery instead of selected and unloadable. If `step-N/` was the run's first permanent checkpoint, the next run would then start from scratch without an error (not tested; unlike item 1, this gives up the old checkpoint). 3. Or do not re-serialize a step that is already committed: skip the forced save when the last save of that step was permanent, as `save_final_checkpoint` does; when it was temporary and in the same directory, wait for that save to finish, then rewrite only `metadata.json` with `is_temporary: false` (through `_save_metadata`), drop the path from `self._temporary_checkpoints` and prune as the permanent-save callback does. PR [#9416](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9416) proposed a skip for the no-op resume and was closed, so 1 or 2 may fit better. ## Prior reports and related issues We found no prior report of this crash consequence. The re-save itself has been reported failing for another reason: - [#9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) (open): "[levanter] Final checkpoint rewrite fails on resume with changed chunk shape". Resuming a run from its final step makes Levanter force another write into the existing `step-N` path, which fails when the resumed run writes a different chunk shape; [#6253](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6253) (closed) had the same failure. PR [#9416](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9416) ("[levanter] Skip checkpoint rewrite on no-op resume") was closed unmerged on 2026-09-25 with the comment "this isn't the right fix, the upstream issue is related to a sharding mismatch", and the open PR [#10786](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10786) proposes a fix for that mismatch. The crash window here does not depend on a layout change: the script above rewrites the same layout. - [#10453](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10453) (open): resuming into a root with uncommitted partial checkpoints fails the next save. A different trigger, but it also comes from saving into a fixed `step-N/` destination; it proposes a fresh directory per save. - [#5386](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5386) (open): retention after a corrupted multihost resume ([#5319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5319)) left one trustworthy permanent checkpoint. A different cause, but it shows the cost when the newest checkpoint cannot be used. - [#2831](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2831) (closed): fault-tolerance validation, which listed "verify async checkpoints are atomic" as a goal. - PR [#9215](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9215): how `metadata.json` is committed on remote storage. - PR [#10969](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10969) (open): lock files for multi-process OCDBT commits on NFS; it also removes `*.__lock` files that a killed process left in a reused `step-N/`. It changes `tensorstore_serialization.py` too, but concerns the OCDBT `manifest.ocdbt`, not `manifest.json`.
Searches (run on 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-12) GitHub issue and pull request search, which `gh search issues` also uses: `repo:marin-community/marin` with `checkpoint manifest.json` (27 results), `temporary checkpoint final save` (79), `checkpoint atomic` (73), `checkpoint corrupt resume` (27), `checkpoint DATA_LOSS` (0), `tensorstore_checkpoint` (0); `repo:marin-community/levanter` with `checkpoint manifest`, `checkpoint corrupt`, `checkpoint atomic`, `checkpoint crash resume`, `temporary checkpoint final` (nothing relevant). Results were read by title, and the candidates above were read in full. Web search: `Levanter checkpoint manifest.json empty CheckpointManifest json_invalid after crash final checkpoint save` (found #2831 and downstream projects' notes on draining asynchronous commits at exit, none about this). On 2026-11-12, threads created since 2026-11-10 (read by title) and issues updated since then with `"final checkpoint"`, `"temporary checkpoint"`, `save_final_checkpoint`, `CheckpointManifest` or `manifest.json`: nothing related.
## How this was found We found this with a crash-injection tool that kills every process with SIGKILL just before or just after each file operation of a checkpoint save, restarts the job with the same configuration and checks what it resumed. The standalone script above reproduces it without that tool. ### AI assistance This report, its reproduction script and the analysis were prepared with an AI coding agent. I ran the reproduction on the versions listed above and checked the analysis and the cited code. If you track such reports with the `agent-generated` label, please add it; I seem unable to set labels.
issues.title: [levanter] A crash during the forced final re-save of a committed `step-N/` can leave it unloadable

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Ablations on Snowball (the 10/05 SFT model) to choose SFT and RL settings for the Mochi 535B post-training run. Each experiment has a 1 h version and an 8 h version. Most backlog items have not run yet; current results are under Status.

## Description

Snowball is a smaller Grug MoE with the same post-training stack as Mochi. Each experiment changes one setting of the SFT or RL recipe (data, optimizer, loss mask, precision, tool format, RL task choice) and compares it against a matched control. The arms are read out with Micro210, BFCL ×5 and a retention panel. Experiments that look useful are then checked on Mochi.

Issue 11177 made the long loop runnable from the 10/05 SFT. Issue 11337 tracks run-ready Snowball recipes and Micro eval scores. Issue 11531 tracks Snowball long-loop SFT on TPU v4.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find which recipe settings change Snowball's agentic and tool-use scores enough to carry into Mochi's next SFT/RL stage.

## Sub-issues

Each result is posted on its own issue:
- Snowball long-loop SFT on TPU v4: issue 11531
- Malformed JSON in nested Pi edit calls: issue 11536
- SFT optimizer, Muon-H vs Adam (C150 vs O150): issue 11537
- TMax data, with vs without: issue 11539
- RL samples per prompt: issue to come
- Mochi BFCL ×5 versus Snowball models: issue 11538

## Status

- **Tool-call format:** see the sub-issue. Malformed nested `edit` calls end more than half of Snowball's SWE trials. An SFT slice of valid nested edits (E12) is trained but not yet read out.
- **SFT optimizer (C150 vs O150):** BFCL ×5 favours Muon-H (30.24% vs 24.55–24.72%, one run each); Micro210 pending. See issue 11537.
- **TMax pair:** held-out TMax loss falls sharply; BFCL ×5 falls vs control. Micro210 pending. See issue 11539.
- **Mochi BFCL ×5 (Pi agent, 123 tasks):** 450/615 record score under the configured retry rule; 449 first-attempt wins, one first-attempt reward unavailable after a timeout.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

- 2026-11-16: Flat edit tool ruled out for reported benchmarks and the default harness. The fix for malformed edits goes on the model side (SFT data).
- 2026-11-16: The SFT training data's tool calls were audited: 452 of 47.4M assistant call spans failed a JSON check. No data repair.

## Conclusion

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 The C150, O150 and TMax SFT arms have trained but still need Micro210 readouts. The E12 one-hour arms also await readout; [#11536](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536) tracks their nested-edit hypothesis. The two published [long-loop recipes](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337) changed training recipes and have different scoring coverage, so their aggregate scores do not isolate an ablation effect.

Plan:
1. For each SFT or RL setting, pin a control and one-setting treatment at the one-hour and eight-hour budgets. Match the starting checkpoint, source and data revisions outside the tested change, task IDs, seeds, Pi harness, and eval policy. Preserve the consumed configs and checkpoint revisions.
2. Finish the pending C150/O150/TMax and E12 one-hour Micro210 readouts first. Compare matching task IDs and report scored/unscored counts, per-benchmark and aggregate deltas, BFCL ×5, and the retention panel. Include malformed nested-edit rates for E12. Use [#11536's gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536): at least a 50% rate reduction against its control with no Micro210 or retention loss.
3. Advance arms with a positive paired agentic/tool-use result and no retention regression to matched eight-hour controls. Repeat the same panels, report uncertainty and incomplete coverage, and record null or adverse results. Check surviving settings on Mochi before selecting its SFT/RL recipe.
4. Keep an arm table here with the changed setting, control and treatment pins, both budget readouts, BFCL and retention results, and the carry/drop decision. Add each run-ready recipe, exact data mix, Micro policy, immutable checkpoint, and archive receipts to [#11337](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337).

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Mochi SFT (step 400407) scores 450/615 = 73.17% on BFCL ×5 with the Pi agent: five runs of 123 tasks each. Snowball models on the same task set and chat template score 33.98–52.36%. The two sets of runs differ in hardware and code version, so the comparison is descriptive, not a controlled test.

## Description

This issue records how Mochi compares with the Snowball models on BFCL ×5, the tool-calling benchmark the Snowball ablations use.
- **Mochi:** the 535B Grug MoE, SFT export at step 400407.
- **Agent:** Pi, the same as the Snowball runs.
- **Serve:** vLLM on four GB200x4 hosts in cw-us-east-08a, with TP1, DP16 and CUDA graphs on.

Parent: issue 11535.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure Mochi's tool-calling score on the benchmark the Snowball ablations use, to anchor what the Snowball results imply for Mochi.

## Status

**Mochi SFT step 400407:**
- **Score:** 92/92/91/86/89 of 123 = 450/615 = 73.17%. This is the record score under the configured Harbor retry rule.
- **First attempts:** 449 first-attempt wins, and one first-attempt reward is unavailable after a timeout. So the first-attempt mean is bounded at 73.01–73.17%.
- **One looping trial:** in run 1, task `bfcl-parallel-multiple-130` looped for 1,800 s with 146 tool turns. Its score comes from a Harbor retry triggered by a verifier timeout.
- **Cost:** 33.52 GB200-h of serving.
- **Retry parity:** the Snowball parent's earlier BFCL ×5 used the same retry rule, with 4 retried trials.

**Snowball models on the same 123 tasks and the training chat template (tools@3f):**

| Model | Score (5 runs) | Run-level bootstrap range | Missing result file (verifier) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mochi SFT step 400407 | 450/615 = 73.17% | not computed | not counted |
| Snowball parent (10/05 SFT) | 322/615 = 52.36% | 50.1–55.6% | 64 |
| Snowball control (15 updates) | 262/615 = 42.60% | 40.2–45.5% | 152 |
| Snowball TMax arm (15 updates) | 209/615 = 33.98% | 31.9–36.1% | 264 |

- **What the ranges mean:** they come from bootstrapping over the 5 runs of a fixed 123-task set. They are not population confidence intervals, and not a test of the difference between models.
- **Missing result file:** this column counts verifier reports that the answer file was absent. It does not say why the file was missing.
- **Snowball cost:** these Snowball runs cost 54.60 H100-h in total.

**Limits:**
- **Environment confound:** Mochi ran on GB200 with a different code version from the Snowball reruns. The Snowball reruns also used a newer runtime than the earlier Snowball runs. Every historical comparison carries this confound, and it cannot isolate the effect of the template or the model.
- **Nested edits:** BFCL does not exercise nested edit calls. Mochi's traces contain only 7 edit calls, none with multiple edits. Issue 11536 tracks that question.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Mochi's 450/615 BFCL ×5 score answers the descriptive benchmark question. The 73.17% versus 33.98–52.36% gap cannot be attributed to the models alone because the serving hardware and code revisions differ; the five-run bootstrap ranges also do not test that gap.

Plan:
1. Link the immutable model checkpoints, evaluation records, source revisions, Pi/Harbor versions, task IDs, seeds, chat template, and retry policy for all four models. Record the missing first-attempt reward and each verifier-missing answer file separately.
2. If a model-effect claim is needed, rerun Mochi and the three Snowball checkpoints on the same hardware and serving/harness revision, using the same 123 tasks, five repetitions, decoding settings, timeouts, and retry policy. Estimate serving cost from the existing runs before launch.
3. Compare paired task outcomes and report both first-attempt and retry-rule scores, scored/missing counts, and uncertainty over tasks. Update this issue's conclusion with the controlled result; keep the current cross-environment scores labeled descriptive.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## Summary
In the Atlas difficulty campaigns, TaskSpec trials whose grading short-circuits without opening a verifier machine (terminal grades and submission rejections, e.g. `GradeResult(GRADED, 0.0, "Missing submission")` and the `SubmissionFailure` path) produce a receipt with `verifier_effective=None`. `network_policy_qualified` (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/harbor/runtime.py`) required `observed.verifier_effective == verifier`, so every such legitimate zero was discarded as `network_policy_violation` and the task ended pending.

Observed in large-v20: six sources (12/79/89/27/51/73 tasks respectively) had all attempts invalidated this way; the verdicts were real zeros (e.g. `{"status": "scored", "reward": 0.0, "detail": {"error": "Text submission requires nonempty assistant content without tool calls"}}`).

## Why the rule can only false-positive here
The recording factory (`_NetworkFactory` in `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/taskcompendium.py`) writes `verifier_effective` exactly when a verifier machine opens, and every machine it opens is created with the declared policy (`verifier_runtime.network` is set from the declaration). So a recorded observation always matches, and an absent observation means no verifier machine ran — the declared policy was vacuously satisfied.

## Fix
Landed on `atlas-env-audit` as 6e33840dd9aa56dc52c9245cebbc8c613955421e: treat an absent verifier observation as qualified, keeping declared-policy drift, runtime-sha drift, and missing mandatory actor observations as failures. Tests in `lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_harbor_runtime.py` cover the machine-less pass, both drift classes, and the mandatory-actor case; `test_oracle_filter.py` regression unchanged.

Requesting review for cherry-pick to main.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`network_policy_qualified` rejects a legitimate zero when grading opens no verifier machine, because the receipt has `verifier_effective=None`. Commit [6e33840](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/6e33840dd9aa56dc52c9245cebbc8c613955421e) fixes this on `atlas-env-audit` and is already included in draft [PR #11277](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11277). Current `main` has neither the TaskSpec runtime module nor the Harbor trial adapter used by that fix; PR #11277 also has merge conflicts, so the commit cannot be landed alone.

**Relevant code**
- [Runtime qualification](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/atlas-env-audit/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/harbor/runtime.py#L115) — accepts absent verifier observations.
- [Harbor receipt recording](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/atlas-env-audit/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/taskcompendium.py#L206) — records policy when a machine opens.
- [Regression tests](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/atlas-env-audit/lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_harbor_runtime.py#L54) — covers machine-less grades and policy drift.

# Proposed Fix

Land this through PR #11277: resolve its conflicts against current `main`, review the TaskSpec runtime and Harbor receipt path together, and run the TaskCompendium and Harbor tests after rebasing. Add `Fixes #11541` to that PR when it is ready to merge. An isolated cherry-pick of 6e33840 would add code without its prerequisite runtime, receipt producer, or qualification callers.
