issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A 15-update SFT arm that swaps part of Snowball's general SFT data for one pass of TMax agent traces fits held-out TMax traces much better. It also scores lower on BFCL ×5 than its matched control, under both chat templates tested. Most of the BFCL drop is attempts where the verifier found no answer file. Micro210 on both arms is pending.

## Description

TMax-15K is a set of agentic terminal traces (bash plus reasoning). This experiment asks whether adding it to Snowball SFT helps or hurts.

Design:
- Both arms start from the 10/05 SFT and train on the same 480 positions of general SFT data.
- The TMax arm replaces 129 of those windows with one pass of TMax traces, which is 27.59% of its supervised targets.
- 15 updates per arm, 64 H100 each.
- Total supervised targets differ between arms. So this tests a replacement package, not a 10% dose or a pure addition.

Parent: issue 11535.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find whether TMax data improves agentic behaviour without costing tool calling or retention, to decide whether it enters the Mochi SFT mix.

## Status

**Held-out TMax traces** (507 traces from 101 held-out tasks; task-macro loss, lower is better):

| | Parent (10/05) | Control (15 updates) | TMax arm (15 updates) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Held-out loss | 0.613 | 0.587 | 0.299 |

- TMax minus control is −0.288 nats, with interval [−0.308, −0.268].
- 74.5% of the gap is in user and system text, not in the assistant turns.
- The parent and control readouts missed an evaluator gate. So this is a sensitivity readout, not a clean acceptance.

**BFCL ×5 (Pi agent, 123 tasks, 5 runs):**

| Chat template | Parent | Control | TMax arm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Earlier inference template | 313/615 = 50.9% | 249/615 = 40.5% | 193/615 = 31.4% |
| Training template (tools@3f, same as Mochi) | 322/615 = 52.36% | 262/615 = 42.60% | 209/615 = 33.98% |

The two template runs used different runtime versions. So the change between rows cannot be attributed to the template alone.

**Why BFCL drops (earlier-template runs, 615 attempts per model):**

| | Parent | Control | TMax arm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Verifier reports the answer file absent | 66 | 149 | 267 |
| Pass rate among attempts with an answer file | 57.0% | 53.4% | 55.5% |

- **What the verifier saw:** the answer file was absent at evaluation time. It does not establish why. Pi logs from these attempts also contain tool errors, so a write-path failure is not ruled out.
- **The conditional pass rate:** it removes an outcome-dependent failure category. So it is arithmetic, not an adjusted accuracy or a treatment comparison.

**Cost:** training 99.95 H100-h for both arms (45.40 control + 54.56 TMax).

**Pending:** Micro210 on both arms. Results will be posted here as a comment.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The 15-update TMax replacement has 53 fewer BFCL successes than its matched control with the training template (209/615 versus 262/615). In the earlier-template runs, the verifier found no answer file in 267 treatment attempts versus 149 control attempts; the logs also contain tool errors, so the failure mechanism is unresolved. Held-out TMax loss is lower, but 74.5% of the treatment-control gap is in user/system text and the parent/control readouts missed an evaluator gate. This is an experiment readout, with no isolated repository defect to fix yet.

# Plan

1. Pin both checkpoints, consumed data manifests and target counts, source revisions, and evaluation policy/commands in the [Snowball recipe ledger](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337). Preserve the 27.59% supervised-target share and the unequal total targets as limits on attribution.
2. Finish the matched Micro210 and retention readouts called for in [the parent ablation issue](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535). Report paired task-level and per-benchmark deltas, scored/unscored counts, aggregate scores, and uncertainty under the same harness, tasks, and seeds.
3. Audit BFCL attempts with absent answer files by task and seed. Use the Pi, tool, sandbox, and verifier records to separate model non-completion from tool/write failures, timeouts, and grading failures. Correct confirmed infrastructure failures before rerunning affected attempts under a pinned runtime; keep model failures in the denominator.
4. Repeat the held-out TMax readout with the evaluator gate satisfied and report assistant-turn loss separately. Use BFCL, Micro210, retention, and the corrected loss readout for the carry/drop decision. Do not advance this replacement mix to Mochi while the BFCL deficit remains unexplained; test a smaller dose or an additive, token-matched mix as a separate ablation if the TMax signal still merits follow-up.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
🤖 An agent literature survey for the Mochi post-training recipe found two Nemotron-sourced changes for train/inference mismatch in async MoE RL. Mochi RL already uses one of them (router replay). The other, an FP32 LM head, has not been tested by us. Nothing here was measured empirically on Mochi: this is a pointer for the RL team, not a result.

**What Nemotron reports**
- The [Nemotron 3.5 Super/Lightning technical report](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-and-Lightning-Technical-Report.pdf) (RL section) says router replay plus an FP32 LM head "reduce the KL error between the training and inference engines by more than an order of magnitude". The two are reported together, so the report does not say how much each one contributes.
- Aside: the [HF MoE handbook](https://huggingface-moe-blogpost.hf.space/) says the NeMo-RL recipes for Nemotron 3 Super/Ultra freeze the router matrix in async RL and keep the load-balancing bias live, and that "whether replay pays off in reward is still contested". Router freezing is an alternative or a complement to replay.

**Where Mochi stands (from existing work, not new measurements)**
- Router replay: Mochi (Hero) RL already uses captured-route replay, and it passed the recorded 4K RL gate in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10388. Its measured replay result is batch-order sensitivity of the gradient: 71.96% → 1.37% at PP48, with +5.3% scoring-plus-update time. That is not a serve-vs-trainer logprob gap, and the same issue notes that serving–trainer differences persist.
- Bit-identical numerics: the stack beginning with https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10634 was closed in favour of score centering with TIS (https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11066, open), with probes in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10658 (open). The Mochi RL launcher is https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11321 (draft).
- FP32 LM head, serving side: the pinned vLLM fork (`0ac9dcb`) already supports it. `vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py` reads `--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'` and accumulates the head GEMM into FP32. Its comment says this is "required for RL training-inference consistency". The Mochi serve config (`experiments/evaluation/mochi/model-mochi-sft-step400407.yaml`) does not set it, so served logits are BF16.
- FP32 LM head, trainer side: SkyRL's Megatron wrapper calls the model with `fp32_output=False` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_model_wrapper.py`), so trainer logits are BF16 too. Matching vLLM would need a Megatron-side FP32 output projection, which is not checked here.
- Related Snowball evidence, not RL and not Mochi: in an Oct 25 Levanter-vs-vLLM scoring check on Snowball, silent MoE token drops and BF16 combine weights were each separate numerics boundaries. Fixing them one at a time cut the p99 per-token logprob gap from 3.96 to 0.60 nats.

**What we did not do:** no empirical study on Mochi of the FP32 head, router freezing, or replay versus no replay. The survey proposed a 1 h arm; it moves off our list and into this issue.

Done when: the RL team decides whether to test an FP32 LM head on both engines (vLLM `head_dtype` plus a Megatron FP32 output projection) on Mochi, measured as the serve-vs-trainer logprob or KL gap on fixed responses with replay on, and records the decision here. Router freezing is optional, as a separate arm.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The draft [Mochi RL recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9/experiments/post_training/mochi_rl/recipe.yaml#L78-L82) enables router replay but has no head-precision override. The [Megatron wrapper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/82cee32cfd5bd479aa0670ba1a92a9c0f96ec4bf/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_model_wrapper.py#L351-L360) passes `fp32_output=False`; [Megatron's implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7c0fac795b76180c26e363fa292c1ce2c025c4df/megatron/core/transformer/module.py#L593-L635) shows that changing this flag only casts outputs after the model forward. [#10388](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10388#issuecomment-6379516756) reports a remaining serving–trainer logprob gap with replay, but no Mochi FP32-head result. The evaluation YAML named above is absent from current `main`; #11321 is the active Mochi recipe.

**Relevant code**
- [Mochi generator config](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9/experiments/post_training/mochi_rl/recipe.yaml#L126-L149) — serving precision insertion point.
- [Megatron wrapper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/82cee32cfd5bd479aa0670ba1a92a9c0f96ec4bf/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_model_wrapper.py#L351-L360) — learner forward path.
- [Pinned vLLM head](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee86ccb447bc717259159c41ad456a/vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py#L142-L177) — FP32 accumulation path.

# Proposed Fix

This needs a paired numerical experiment before a production change. If the RL team allocates the run, use one immutable Mochi checkpoint and fixed responses, routes, replay setting, weights, and scoring layout. Measure four arms: BF16 on both engines, FP32 serving only, FP32 learner only, and FP32 on both. Wire and verify vLLM `hf_overrides: {head_dtype: float32}` in #11321, and implement a genuine FP32-output Megatron head projection; verify its GEMM output precision and backward path rather than relying on `fp32_output=True`.

For each arm, report chosen-token logprob-gap RMS/p99/max, same-token probability-ratio outliers, scorer/serve throughput, and memory, with run IDs and source revisions. Compute full-distribution KL only if full-vocabulary logits are captured. Record the RL team's go/no-go decision against the measured parity gain and cost here; treat router freezing as a separate arm.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

**Latest cross-domain result:** four clear reviews remain correct in all 64 formatting conditions, but two ambiguous reviews exhibit semantic flips in 6/16 class-mapping pairs. The same mixed-feelings review changes from negative to positive solely when the option meanings are swapped (conditional P(positive) 21.44% to 53.22%, B preferred both times). This is an intuitive non-DNA example of mapping sensitivity, not a clear-sentiment accuracy failure. VEP still prefers B in 32/32 contexts even when the response instruction says “B or A,” ruling out a simple last-mentioned-label explanation. [Report and exact prompts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f0e1d8d29ee2e5427c8eca14dff7a34df6ee1c9f/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/cross-domain-report.md).

Evaluate Marin Hero on variant effect prediction using unconditioned DNA likelihood, healthy-individual conditioning, and zero-/two-shot classification. The same 100-variant autosomal missense pilot has completed raw v3 and chat-prefill classification. Reserved 300-variant validation remains unrun. This is a research-branch experiment; no PR or main merge is planned.

Latest chat-prefill AUPRC is **0.157 zero-shot, 0.118 two-shot**, versus historical raw **0.110 / 0.101**; bootstrap intervals do not establish a gain, and serving builds differ. DNA likelihood results remain **0.213 null / 0.302 healthy**, also exploratory. Chat-prefill puts 94.5% / 98.1% probability on A/B, but zero-shot prefers B in all 200 VEP contexts. [100-variant chat report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f0ccf14940ab3f7b286bc19c1382b5e0c5823caa/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/chat-pilot-report.md).

**The small non-DNA diagnostic rules out a universal B preference on these tested inputs:** the same prefill answers 24/24 easy contexts correctly under swapped labels; native short-answer chat answers 21/24 correctly. Unknown-outcome controls prefer B 3/8 and the first-listed option 7/8. VEP B preference is moderate (conditional B probability median 62.1%, range 54.9–77.0%), not near-certainty. Its prompt/task-specific cause remains unresolved; no general training defect or need for additional training is established. [Diagnostic report and exact evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5de5167a6beddbc0a8183bf0ef597c72b4b6de7c/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/easy-diagnostic-report.md).

**Earlier VEP-specific control:** fully crossed four-variant probe prefers B in 32/32 A/B contexts and D in 31/32 C/D contexts, including both list orders and real/shuffled DNA. Swapping class-to-letter mapping changes the semantic prediction in 31/32 pairs; median absolute conditional pathogenic-probability change is 24.05 points for mapping versus 2.10 for flank shuffling. This is strong prompt-dependent label sensitivity, not universal B preference. At that stage, instruction mention order was confounded with alphabetic order; the subsequent cross-domain control above separates mention order for A/B. [Completed diagnostic](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/17cff78cfa70bfe4c8e3d82308686caec3a17430/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/vep-factor-report.md).

## Scope: experiment only

This issue tracks a research experiment, not a production feature or a contribution to `main`. Keep experimental code, prompts, analysis, and evidence on the research and harness branches. Opening or reopening PRs, merging code or the archive index into `main`, and production integration are out of scope. Any later promotion requires a separate decision and explicit authorization.

Completion means recording the experiment's results, limitations, and conclusions with reproducible branch-based evidence. It does not require a PR, code review approval, or a merge. Marin PR #11375 and marin-community/marin-logbooks#41 were closed without merging; their branches and commits remain available.

## Description

This experiment measures variant effect prediction (VEP) capability in the Marin Hero SFT model.
MarinDNA supplies the dataset and reference evaluation protocol; VEP-bench supplies the classification input representation.
The pilot supports prompt and scoring iteration before a frozen-method comparison on a fresh, larger development subset.

### Dataset and reference scoring protocol

Reuse the dataset and scoring conventions from the Mendelian evaluation in [Open-Athena/marin-dna](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/tree/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2) as the reference.

- Dataset: `marin-dna/evals_mendelian_traits`, revision `4aed58e50c5dea0b878a665007af2ef9e5108e9f`.
- Split: `train`, which is the project's development split.
- Positives: pathogenic SNVs from OMIM, HGMD, and Smedley et al. 2016, with allele frequency below 0.1%.
- Controls: gnomAD variants with allele frequency above 0.1%.
- Matching: one positive and nine controls per `match_group`, matched within consequence/chromosome strata using distance features.
- Standard likelihood score: compute `LLR = log P(alt) - log P(ref)` for each strand, average forward and reverse-complement LLRs, then negate the average so larger scores indicate predicted pathogenicity.
- Established reporting: per-consequence, global, and macro-average AUPRC, with match-group bootstrap uncertainty.

The DNA-model kernel uses a four-nucleotide softmax and single-base tokens.
Hero's general-vocabulary token likelihoods define a related but different scoring protocol; do not claim numerical parity with that kernel.

### Pilot sample

Use ten complete missense match groups: 100 variants comprising ten pathogenic positives and 90 matched controls.
The two few-shot demonstrations are additional development examples, separate from these 100 evaluation variants.
Use autosomes only (chromosomes 1–22) throughout demonstrations, pilot queries, sensitivity checks, and fresh development validation. Exclude chromosome X before constructing any sampling pools.

Before selecting rows:

1. Verify the dataset's missense consequence label and select only missense groups.
2. Check eligible group counts and preserve complete groups.
3. Select deterministically with a recorded seed, without using model scores.
4. Record variant IDs, genomic build and coordinates, reference/alternate alleles, consequence labels, group IDs, source revision, and sequence checksums.
5. Verify reference alleles against the genome and extract centered 255-base windows: 127 bases on either side of the SNV.
6. Prepare both forward and reverse-complement inputs, transforming allele and position descriptions consistently.

Use the same pilot variants for every approach.
Draw few-shot examples from a separate part of the development split, excluding pilot groups, duplicate variants, and overlapping windows.
Prefer chromosome-disjoint example/query pools where the available missense groups permit it; record the actual separation used.
Do not use the held-out test split for prompt selection or development evaluation.

### Approaches to compare

Let `L_c(s)` be the sum of log probabilities of the DNA tokens in sequence `s`, conditional on prefix `c`.
Exclude the prefix itself and any EOS probability from this score.
For reference/alternate contrasts, retain identical conditioning text and use summed likelihoods rather than means over variable numbers of BPE tokens.
Define token-boundary handling explicitly before execution.

#### Template conventions

The following templates define the current v3 comparison. Historical v1/v2 templates and results remain archived at their original commits.

- Replace `{sequence}` with either the reference or alternate 255-base window, in separate requests.
- DNA is uppercase, on one line, with no spaces.
- Likelihood inputs have no trailing newline; classification FASTA records have a newline before their closing code fence.
- `{reference_sequence}` is the complete reference window for a classification query; its alternate allele is specified by the compact VCF row.
- `{ref_base}` and `{alt_base}` are the alleles in the displayed orientation.
- Position 128 is 1-based within the displayed 255-base window, including after reverse complementation.
- Braces denote substitution placeholders and are not sent literally.
- Newlines shown inside templates are literal.
- Outer four-backtick fences delimit the classification templates; the inner FASTA/VCF three-backtick fences are literal model input.
- VCF columns are separated by literal tabs; each record uses synthetic contig `sequence` and local coordinates.
- No gene name, genomic coordinate, consequence category, or true query label is included in the query text.

#### 1. Unprompted sequence likelihood

Exact input template, used once for the reference and once for the alternate:

```text
{sequence}
```

There is no text before the DNA and no trailing newline.
Score all DNA tokens, excluding any BOS or EOS target.
Score `L_empty(ref) - L_empty(alt)` on each strand and average.
This is the basic Hero VEP baseline.

#### 2. Healthy-individual prefix

Exact input template, used once for the reference and once for the alternate:

```text
The following sequence is from a healthy individual:
{sequence}
```

The prefix ends in exactly one newline after the colon.
There is no trailing newline after the DNA.
Score only the DNA continuation, excluding the sentence and its newline.
Verify that tokenization permits this scoring boundary; do not silently include a token spanning prefix text and DNA in the DNA-only score.

Score `L_healthy(ref) - L_healthy(alt)` on each strand and average.
The likelihood comparison has exactly two prefix conditions: no text prefix and this healthy-individual prefix.

#### 3. Zero-shot classification (v3)

Use one fixed, seeded answer mapping per variant, shared across zero-shot, two-shot and both strands. Seed 11181 ranks variant identities by SHA-256, independently of labels; each panel is split exactly in half between A=pathogenic/B=benign and A=benign/B=pathogenic. The [mapping manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c66cf85742e51f037e921993d0b7eda3aff46b3b/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/answer-mappings-v2.json) records all assignments: 50/50 for the pilot and 150/150 for validation.

In both templates, substitute `{class_A}`/`{class_B}` with the assigned labels. The final query prompt ends exactly at `Answer:` with no trailing space or newline. Candidate completions are ` A` and ` B`, including their leading space. Demonstrated answers retain the same visible `Answer: A` / `Answer: B` format.

````text
Classify single-nucleotide variants for Mendelian disease.
Each FASTA contains a 255-base reference DNA sequence.
Each compact VCF describes one substitution in its accompanying sequence.
POS is 1-based relative to that sequence, not a genomic coordinate.
REF and ALT use the displayed sequence orientation.
A: {class_A}
B: {class_B}
Respond with exactly one letter: A or B.

Query:
```fasta
>sequence
{reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{ref_base}	{alt_base}
```
Which classification applies to variant V01 in the query?
Answer:
````

Tokenize the complete prefix-plus-candidate and require an unchanged prefix followed by exactly one answer token. On the tested tokenizer, ` A`=362 and ` B`=426. Request both IDs in one unmasked next-token response (`logprob_token_ids`, `max_tokens=1`); ignore the sampled token. Small live parity checks matched separate teacher-forced scores exactly. Never force a standalone-space token followed by bare A/B.

Compute `log P(pathogenic letter) - log P(benign letter)` under the assigned mapping and average the two strands. There is one benchmark score per method, not a mapping-average score. Both-mapping checks belong only in a small separate diagnostic subset.

#### 4. Two-shot classification (v3)

Insert exactly the two fixed labeled demonstrations into the same template. Their answer letters follow the query's assigned mapping. Instructions, option placement, query bytes and answer suffix remain identical to zero-shot; removing only the example section produces the zero-shot prompt byte-for-byte.

````text
Classify single-nucleotide variants for Mendelian disease.
Each FASTA contains a 255-base reference DNA sequence.
Each compact VCF describes one substitution in its accompanying sequence.
POS is 1-based relative to that sequence, not a genomic coordinate.
REF and ALT use the displayed sequence orientation.
A: {class_A}
B: {class_B}
Respond with exactly one letter: A or B.

Example 1:
```fasta
>sequence
````

### Shared-prefix caching and tokenization

Rely on vLLM's automatic prefix caching when enabled and supported by the scoring request path; do not implement a separate client-side KV cache.
For a centered SNV, the reference and alternate share the left flank:

```text
reference = left flank + reference allele + right flank
alternate = left flank + alternate allele + right flank
```

The shared prefix's likelihood cancels in the reference/alternate difference.
Both the variant and downstream sequence must still be scored: identical downstream letters have different conditioning histories after the mutation.
Cache reuse operates on identical token prefixes, so a base-level mutation can also change the boundary of the reusable token prefix.

The distinction to verify is between normal next-token scoring and requesting log probabilities for tokens already in the prompt:

- **A/B classification:** prefer obtaining both candidate probabilities from the next-token distribution without asking for all prompt logprobs, if the endpoint supports it.
  Repeated few-shot demonstrations can then benefit from the server's normal prefix caching.
- **DNA likelihood:** the straightforward `echo`/prompt-logprob route requests scores throughout the input.
  The current vLLM V1 guide states that such requests bypass prefix-cache reads and recompute the prompt, even with prefix caching enabled.
  Verify the deployed build's behavior rather than assuming the shared half is reused.

Before the pilot, verify tokenization and scoring boundaries and check available cache metrics for the actual request path.
Use server-managed reuse where available; a correct uncached baseline is acceptable for this 100-variant pilot, with its runtime recorded.
Consider a supported selective-scoring interface only if necessary for subsequent scaling, and validate score parity before adoption.

### Execution and completion criteria

1. **Prepare inputs and scoring definitions.**
   Verify missense membership, freeze the 100-variant sample and two-demonstration manifests, and save exact prompt templates.
2. **Validate a few pairs.**
   Inspect sequence construction, token boundaries, score signs, both strands, and actual caching behavior; check parity if using a selective-scoring path.
3. **Run the small development pilot.**
   Apply all four approaches to the same subset with bounded concurrency, request limits, and a recorded endpoint-use budget.
   Confirm these execution limits before launch; this draft does not launch a sweep or provision compute.
4. **Inspect and iterate.**
   Save per-variant reference/alternate likelihoods, classification scores, strand disagreement, prompt sensitivity, errors, latency, and token/cache accounting.
   Inspect within-group pathogenic-versus-control ranking and representative failure cases.
   AUPRC on ten positives is exploratory; the pilot does not meet the existing evaluator's 30-group threshold for standard per-subset reporting.
5. **Freeze and validate more broadly.**
   Freeze templates, demonstrations, score formulas, and selection rules before evaluating a fresh, larger development subset.
   Use established consequence-stratified metrics and paired match-group resampling to compare methods where sample size supports it.

Preserve raw scoring outputs and request metadata so scores can be recomputed without rerunning inference.
Keep pilot tuning results distinct from the later frozen-method validation results.
Do not describe this pilot as clinical validation or as an official benchmark result.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Determine whether Marin Hero ranks pathogenic missense variants above matched common controls using sequence likelihood alone, and whether healthy-individual conditioning or labeled demonstrations improve those rankings.
Compare all four approaches on the same 100 variants, preserving forward/reverse-complement scores and matched groups.
The pilot can expose scoring failures and prompt sensitivity; ten positive variants are insufficient for a reliable benchmark claim.

### Rank and batching diagnosis (November 13)

The service uses unquantized BF16 with data/expert parallelism. The supported `X-data-parallel-rank` header isolated two effects:

- Across four selected ranks, two fixed prompts repeated three times each were exactly stable within each rank but differed between ranks (24 completions).
- On fixed rank 0, all 36 targets covering two autosomal variants, both strands, all four methods and an explicit-pair format check matched exactly across two sequential passes. A four-client pass changed the same targets, by up to 5.6548 DNA log-likelihood units and 0.6612 classification-token log-probability units (108 completions total).
- A final sequential pass after concurrent traffic recovered all 36 original scores exactly.

**Bounded workaround:** pin one rank and serialize calls, with repeated sentinels. This worked in these checks but other traffic on a shared expert-parallel service can still affect batching. Repeatability is distinct from model correctness.

**Durable fix to test:** `serve.vllm_batch_invariant: true` on an approved scoring service, followed by rank/batch/order repeatability checks and performance measurement. Hero/GrugMoE is not among the deployed version's documented validated models; the flag is not a verified fix yet. Preserve compilation and CUDA graphs. If it fails, compare replicated parameter hashes and intermediate activations across ranks to localize the kernel/reduction. The newer serving release's documented fixes do not establish a fix for this BF16 prefill discrepancy.

- [Dataset descriptions](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/dashboard/src/data/datasets.json.py)
- [vLLM automatic prefix caching](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/automatic_prefix_caching/)
- [vLLM V1 prompt-logprob behavior](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/v1_guide/#prompt-logprobs-with-prefix-caching)
- [Newer selective prompt scoring documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/training/prompt_token_id_logprobs/)
- [VEP-bench FASTA/VCF prompt representation](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/blob/205df32032b9ff6be11bc387879e8bed578839aa/configs/tasks/sge/prompt.yaml)


## Decision Log

- November 16, cross-domain controls: ambiguous reviews reproduce mapping sensitivity outside DNA; all clear-review conditions succeed. VEP B preference survives B-or-A instruction order. Report a prompt-dependent robustness issue, not universal B bias or a proven training defect; keep validation unrun.

- November 16, crossed VEP controls: later label B/D wins 63/64 despite list-order reversal; mapping changes semantic preference 31/32. Do not scale classification yet. Instruction mention order remains unresolved; no additional control run launched.

- November 16: completed chat-prefill pilot and 56-response easy/unknown diagnostic. Universal B preference and universal B fallback under uncertainty are not supported. Keep VEP-specific prompt/order/content causes unresolved; no training intervention or larger run is authorized by this result. Preserve both native errors and prefill successes.

- November 13 (v3): canonical leading-space answer tokens, one joint response per A/B pair, same seeded mappings and shared template. Complete pilot: AUPRC 0.110 zero-shot and 0.101 two-shot. No post-hoc sign flips. General-language-model peers only; prioritize likelihood scoring.
- November 13 (v2, superseded after EOS diagnosis): condition on the trailing space and score bare A/B; use one seeded balanced mapping per variant; use an identical zero-/two-shot template except for demonstrations. Implemented and smoke-verified; supersedes the v1 freeze. Preserve v1 results separately.

- November 13: freeze all four original primary methods, score signs, templates, demonstrations and both-strand averages after pilot analysis. Keep mapping averages secondary; do not select a mapping or flip score signs to improve pilot performance.

- November 13: keep this work as a branch-based experiment. Contributions or merges into `main` are out of scope; both PRs are closed with branches preserved.

- November 13: proceed on the available final Hero SFT step-400407 checkpoint, replacing the earlier quick-SFT feasibility model. Preserve the checkpoint distinction in all results.
- Use 100 missense variants: ten complete match groups, with ten positives and 90 controls.
- Compare exactly two DNA-likelihood prefixes: no text prefix and the healthy-individual sentence.
- Use FASTA/VCF classification inputs with synthetic contig `sequence`, A/B answer likelihoods, and a reversed-label sensitivity check.
- Use only autosomes throughout. Reserve chromosome 1 for two separate missense demonstrations, one pathogenic and one control; query groups use other autosomes. Fix selection and demonstration order with seed 11181.
- Reserve 30 complete fresh development groups (300 variants) for validation after freezing the protocol. Exclude pilot overlaps and keep the held-out test split unused.
- Rely on server-managed prefix caching where supported; verify the scoring request path and allow an uncached pilot baseline.
- Keep service URLs, deployment identifiers, and access instructions outside the public issue.

## Conclusion

**Latest cross-domain result:** four clear reviews remain correct in all 64 formatting conditions, but two ambiguous reviews exhibit semantic flips in 6/16 class-mapping pairs. The same mixed-feelings review changes from negative to positive solely when the option meanings are swapped (conditional P(positive) 21.44% to 53.22%, B preferred both times). This is an intuitive non-DNA example of mapping sensitivity, not a clear-sentiment accuracy failure. VEP still prefers B in 32/32 contexts even when the response instruction says “B or A,” ruling out a simple last-mentioned-label explanation. [Report and exact prompts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f0e1d8d29ee2e5427c8eca14dff7a34df6ee1c9f/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/cross-domain-report.md).

**Earlier VEP-specific control:** fully crossed four-variant probe prefers B in 32/32 A/B contexts and D in 31/32 C/D contexts, including both list orders and real/shuffled DNA. Swapping class-to-letter mapping changes the semantic prediction in 31/32 pairs; median absolute conditional pathogenic-probability change is 24.05 points for mapping versus 2.10 for flank shuffling. This is strong prompt-dependent label sensitivity, not universal B preference. At that stage, instruction mention order was confounded with alphabetic order; the subsequent cross-domain control above separates mention order for A/B. [Completed diagnostic](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/17cff78cfa70bfe4c8e3d82308686caec3a17430/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/vep-factor-report.md).

Chat-prefill improves A/B answer-format compliance, but a VEP-performance improvement is not established. The easy-question diagnostic gets 24/24 correct with the same prefill and both answer assignments, so the VEP B preference should not be described as a universal model defect. Unknown-outcome controls also do not show universal B fallback. Native short-answer errors suggest additional format/order sensitivity; the VEP-specific mechanism remains unresolved. [Completed diagnostic](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5de5167a6beddbc0a8183bf0ef597c72b4b6de7c/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/easy-diagnostic-report.md).

DNA likelihood remains a promising direction in this exploratory ten-group pilot, with the healthy-prefix benefit still uncertain. General-language-model comparisons require a stable likelihood-scoring path. Reserved validation remains unrun. Research branch only; production integration, PRs and merging into main remain out of scope.

issues.title: Experiment: evaluate Marin Hero on variant effect prediction

issues.author: rdolmedo
issues.body:
🤖 Pre-registered prediction of Snowball's AAI-open score after SFT on a synthetic mixture that targets the AAI-open benchmarks, made from smaller scales: the Snowflakes and Snowball's step-18000 checkpoint. It was recorded before any Snowball result was looked at. We follow the broad methodology of #11381. The predictions and figures follow in the next comments.

## What is AAI-open?

AAI-open is an open reproduction of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0); we will release it soon. Each AA v5.0 slot keeps its weight. Where AA's benchmark is private, an open benchmark from Index v4.3 takes its place.

| AA v5.0 slot | Weight | AAI-open benchmark (items × attempts) |
|---|---|---|
| AA-Briefcase | 15 | GDPval-AA, Elo against reference runs (185 tasks), scored 100 · clamp((Elo − 500) / 2000) |
| FrontierCode | 15 | SciCode, main-problem accuracy (60 problems × 6) |
| Terminal-Bench-Science | 15 | TB-Science lite (32 × 2) |
| Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 10 | Terminal-Bench 2.1 (84 × 3) |
| CritPt | 10 | CritPt (70 × 3) |
| AA-Omniscience | 10 + 5 | AA-Omniscience public set, accuracy + non-hallucination rate (300 × 3) |
| HLE-Diamond | 10 | HLE-Diamond, text-only (157 × 2) |
| AutomationBench | 5 | AutomationBench public set (446 × 1) |
| GDP.pdf | 5 | GDP.pdf, text-only (37 × 2) |

- The agentic benchmarks (the Terminal-Benches, AutomationBench, CritPt, GDPval) run in the Pi agent harness with a 131K context and no compaction. Reasoning is on.
- HLE, Omniscience and GDP.pdf are judged by Qwen3.8-27B. CritPt's official grader is private, so it is scored by agreement with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's answers.
- GDPval is scored as an Elo: Qwen3.8-27B compares each deliverable with those of two reference models (Qwen3.8 27B Xhigh and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning), and the Elo enters the Briefcase slot through the transform above. Every other slot is a raw percentage.
- To speed up evaluation, the test sets are subsampled, and not at random: for most benchmarks we dropped the items that none of 8 open reference models ever solved. HLE and GDPval use random subsets; CritPt and Omniscience keep every item.
- The SFT evaluations in this issue also cap each benchmark's response length at Nemotron Super's 95th-percentile test length.

Open models, scored on the current leaderboard setup:

| Model | AAI-open | AA Index v4.3.2 (Oct 2026) | AA Index v5.0 (Nov 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) | 41.6 | 45.1 | 32.6 |
| Qwen3.8 27B (Xhigh) | 31.2 | 33.7 | 20.1 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super VL | 30.6 | 26.5 | 13.6 |
| Qwen3.8 27B (Medium) | 26.9 | 27.6 | 17.5 |
| Qwen3.6 35B A3B | 19.2 | 18.2 | – |
| Gemma 4 26B A4B | 17.1 | 16.7 | – |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning | 14.1 | 12.9 | 5.5 |
| Qwen3.5 4B | 6.3 | 13.1 | – |

Absolute AAI-open numbers are not a reflection of the AA Index (they sit near v4.3 and 9–17 points above v5.0); AAI-open serves as a compass for model development.

## What is the SFT dataset?

The tasks are synthetic and generated by DeepSeek from a taxonomy of each benchmark's task types; the trajectories come from Nemotron 3.5 Super. Each of the nine AAI-open benchmarks gets about 1/9 of the tokens; both Omniscience slots share one part, and the Terminal-Bench part reuses the TB SFT data of #11381. 🤖 From loss to scores. For each benchmark, we fit a one-parameter IRT model to the per-item responses of six SFT'd models: Snowball at 7% of training (step-18000) after 1B, 3B and 9B SFT tokens, and the three Snowflakes. Item difficulties are calibrated on all six models and integrated out. issues.author: ravwojdyla
issues.body:
`data-belay check` and `prepare` use the datasets-server row count even when the response is marked `partial: true`. For `mlfoundations/dclm-baseline-1.0`, the server reports 779,982 rows. The dataset has about 3B rows and about 4T tokens. `check` estimates 1.0B tokens, reports 0.56 epochs at d1024, and passes the dataset.

`prepare` then computes tokens per byte as that estimate divided by the 7.2 TB of data files (`experiments/data_belay/prepare.py:82`). The ratio is about 4,000× too low, so `select_files` (`prepare.py:49`) picks 25,780 of 27,838 files, about 6.7 TB, to cover a d1024 need of 0.58B tokens. The row cap does not limit the total, because `tokenize` applies it per shard (`take_per_shard`, `lib/marin/src/marin/processing/tokenize/_core.py:406`). The job would download and tokenize most of DCLM from Hugging Face.

Reproduce:
1. `uv run data-belay check --dataset mlfoundations/dclm-baseline-1.0 --share 0.2`
2. The output shows `size: 779,982 rows, about 1,030,517,288 tokens` and `passed`.
3. `curl 'https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/size?dataset=mlfoundations/dclm-baseline-1.0'` returns `"partial": true`.

Expected: intake refuses a partial row count, or sizes the dataset from its file bytes, so `check` reports the real size and `prepare` selects only the files it needs.

`_num_rows` (`experiments/data_belay/intake.py:187`) reads `size.splits[].num_rows` and ignores the top-level `partial` flag. `math-ai/AutoMathText` also returns `partial: true`. FinePDFs and Zyda-2 return complete counts.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

`_num_rows` sums `size.splits[].num_rows` without checking the response's top-level `partial` flag. `run_intake` uses that count for the token estimate, which `prepare` converts to tokens per file byte; a partial count can therefore select most of a large dataset.

**Relevant code**
- [`intake.py#L187-L197`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5/experiments/data_belay/intake.py#L187-L197) — reads the row count
- [`intake.py#L261-L277`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5/experiments/data_belay/intake.py#L261-L277) — estimates tokens
- [`prepare.py#L79-L95`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5/experiments/data_belay/prepare.py#L79-L95) — selects files

**Proposed Fix**

Reject a size response marked `partial: true` before using its split counts. A regression test will cover partial and complete responses; `check` and `prepare` will then refuse the reported incomplete count.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
🤖 A multi-node vLLM data-parallel serve can die during startup when flashinfer downloads a cubin header on a cold node. One worker holds the download lock longer than 30 s, the other workers on that node give up, and the engine fails with `AssertionError: flashInferMetaInfo.h not found`. The other engines then wait forever, and every Iris task still reads `running`.

This affects any DP serve that starts on a node with an empty flashinfer cache, not only the Mochi serve where we saw it.

Reproduce (intermittent; depends on download speed):
1. Start the Mochi SFT serve (DP16 EP, 4 x GB200x4, cw-us-east-08a, flashinfer 0.6.18.post1) on nodes with an empty `/root/.cache/flashinfer`.
2. During `capture_model(profile_only=True)`, the four workers on one node fetch `fmha/trtllm-gen/include/flashInferMetaInfo.h`.

Expected: every worker gets the header and the serve becomes ready.

Observed on 2026-11-16 (log excerpt in a [secret gist](https://gist.github.com/karansag/528ef1da72eee0721d8342081e97e77f)):
- 22:41:58 DP11 acquired the lock and began the download from the NVIDIA cubin CDN.
- 22:42:29–22:42:34 DP8, DP10 and DP9 logged `Failed to acquire lock … within 30 seconds`, then asserted. The engine core for that node failed with `Worker failed with error 'flashInferMetaInfo.h not found'`.
- DP12 on another node also hit the lock timeout but survived, so the failure depends on timing.
- The two earlier serves of the same model and image came up normally.

Cause: in flashinfer `jit/cubin_loader.py`, `download_file` waits a fixed 30 s for the per-file lock (`lock_timeout=30`, not configurable through callers). On timeout it returns `False`, `get_artifact` returns empty bytes, and `jit/attention/modules.py` fails `assert metainfo`. Upstream [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3507](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3507) reports duplicate concurrent downloads. [PR 6461](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6461) makes waiting workers reuse a finished download, but the 30 s timeout still returns `False`.

Possible fixes, from least to most change:
- Prefetch the needed cubins once per node before the vLLM workers start, or point `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` at a prefilled directory.
- Install the `flashinfer-cubin` package in the serve image so no download happens; `FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD` then turns a missing file into a clear error ([TRT-LLM notes](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/docs/source/llm-api/index.md#flashinfer-jit-workspaces-for-mpi-workers)).

Cost of this occurrence: 3.61 GB200-hours. Related: issue 11536.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 waits only 30 seconds for the per-artifact lock; a timeout returns no header and aborts worker startup. Marin has two GPU launch paths: `--task-image` uses the image's preinstalled vLLM, while the isolated CUDA launcher installs vLLM and compiler packages but no matching FlashInfer cubin wheel. The [0.6.18.post1 release](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/v0.6.18.post1) provides a 1.56 GB cubin wheel; [FlashInfer's installation guidance](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/docs/installation.rst) requires a wheel matching `flashinfer-python`. No open Marin PR overlaps this issue.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris_cli.py#L171-L176`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py#L171-L176) — task images select preinstalled vLLM.
- [`vllm_server.py#L145-L158`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_server.py#L145-L158) — preinstalled launcher uses image dependencies.
- [`vllm_server.py#L222-L245`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_server.py#L222-L245) — isolated CUDA install omits cubins.

# Proposed Fix

1. Identify the failed serve's task image digest and launcher. In that exact runtime, record `flashinfer show-config`, `flashinfer-python`/`flashinfer-cubin` versions, and whether `fmha/trtllm-gen/include/flashInferMetaInfo.h` is packaged. This determines which launch path needs the first change.
2. Put the version-matched cubin wheel in the GPU task image during its build, or provision it before vLLM starts for the isolated CUDA path. Use FlashInfer's wheel index or `flashinfer download-kernels`; PyPI's `flashinfer-cubin` is stale. Pin the version and verify the header is available with an empty runtime cache. Cover both launch paths if both can run multi-worker GPU serves.
3. On one cold GB200x4 node, start four workers concurrently and verify readiness without a cubin CDN fetch. Then run the DP16/EP configuration once and verify all engines become ready. If one worker fails, verify the Iris job reaches a terminal failure instead of leaving every task `running`; fix failure propagation if that check fails.

The GPU task-image build is not in this repository, and this plan requires a cold-cache GPU validation, so a Marin-only launcher edit would not establish a fix for the reported serve.

issues.author: asartran
issues.body:
Minerva symbolic answer comparison in taskcompendium scores correct answers as wrong when many comparisons run at once. The nightly CI `slow` job has failed on this since Nov 4, and under real concurrent grading the same path would silently score equivalent answers 0 instead of raising an error.

`test_minerva_concurrent_workers_complete_symbolic_matches` (`lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_evalchemy_math.py:72-77`) runs `is_equiv(r"\sqrt{4}", "2")` from 48 threads and expects 48 `True` results. Every nightly run since Nov 4 returns 48 `False`, in 13-14 s:

```
FAILED lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_evalchemy_math.py::test_minerva_concurrent_workers_complete_symbolic_matches
E   assert [False, False...e, False, ...] == [True, True, ...ue, True, ...]
```

From a worker thread, `_sympy_is_equiv` (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/minerva.py:178-221`) runs the comparison in a fresh process through `call_bounded`, with 30 s for startup plus the 5 s `_SYMPY_TIMEOUT`. Inside that process, the 5 s `SIGALRM` covers the first `parse_latex` call, which also loads SymPy's ANTLR LaTeX parser. That first parse takes 0.4-1.0 s on an idle core (measured on a development machine); 48 processes on the runner's 4 vCPUs leave about 12 per core, so the alarm likely fires and `except TimeoutError: return False` scores the pair as a non-match. The 13-14 s test duration is well under the 35 s outer limit, which points at the inner alarm rather than worker startup. I have not confirmed this inside the CI runner.

Reproduce:
1. On a 4-vCPU machine, run `uv run --package marin-taskcompendium --group test pytest -m slow lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_evalchemy_math.py::test_minerva_concurrent_workers_complete_symbolic_matches`.
2. Or see any nightly "Marin - Unit" run since Nov 4, for example https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43463378903 (job `slow`).

Expected: equivalent answers compare `True` when comparisons run concurrently, as the test asserts, so a busy grader does not score correct answers 0 because of parser start-up time.

The test and the bounded worker came in with #10757.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`is_equiv` sends symbolic comparisons from grading threads through `call_bounded`. The child arms a five-second wall-clock `SIGALRM` before its first LaTeX parse; under the nightly job's 48-way concurrency, time spent waiting for CPU can exhaust that alarm and is returned as `False`. The repeated CI result supports this path, though the runner has no per-worker timeout trace.

**Relevant code**
- [`minerva.py#L178-L223`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/minerva.py#L178-L223) — worker dispatch and alarm
- [`worker.py#L22-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/execution/worker.py#L22-L49) — outer wall deadline
- [`test_evalchemy_math.py#L72-L77`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_evalchemy_math.py#L72-L77) — 48-worker regression

# Proposed Fix

`is_equiv` → `call_bounded` → `_sympy_is_equiv` currently counts scheduler delay against SymPy's five-second limit and turns that timeout into a non-match. Use a CPU-time timer for the comparison, retain the worker's 35-second wall deadline, and report an exhausted outer deadline as `GradingInfraError` so overload cannot silently assign a zero.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 Fix proposed in #11428. Isolated Minerva workers now count comparison CPU time, and an exhausted subprocess wall deadline raises `GradingInfraError` instead of assigning a zero. The focused safe tests pass (12/12); the 48-worker regression remains in nightly CI. The broader safe suite had 703 passes and four fixture errors because this host's Python lacks `os.pidfd_open`.

🤖 **November 14 triage:** [SkyRL nightly run 43610622635](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43610622635) passed OPD and CatCount. Grug Megatron reached its GPU suite and failed `test_grug_megatron_train_forward_matches_eval_forward[snowball_like_top4_long-pp2_ep2]` after 20 passes. The [native log artifact](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43610622635/artifacts/14120985695) records mean absolute train/eval log-ratio 0.000494 and maximum 0.063827, above the test's 0.001 maximum. The Iris job failed because pytest exited 1; there is no placement, preemption, log-read, or lock failure in this run. The [November 13 nightly](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43467677695) passed the same lane, so this failure was intermittent on the current profile.

**Cause and fix:** The [test config at the failing revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e9ae26899c90512195e68f0edec808bb42b88bf3/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/tests/gpu/test_grug_megatron.py#L164-L175) uses BF16 with `flash_attn=False`; the [worker selects fused attention](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e9ae26899c90512195e68f0edec808bb42b88bf3/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_worker.py#L139-L160). [Draft PR #11307](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11307) already changes BF16 Grug to select FlashAttention and reports H100 training/evaluation checks within this tolerance. That is the existing repository fix for the observed mismatch; the precise kernel-level source of the intermittent drift is not isolated. A second PR would duplicate it.

Keep #10910 open until #11307 lands and a subsequent nightly passes all three lanes. The PR is still draft and needs review; no Iris infrastructure issue is indicated by this failure.

spillover_issues.author: code259
spillover_issues.body:
## Context

Following a discussion with @penfever in the Marin Discord, I'm interested in contributing to agentic mid-training data preparation, starting with AgentTrove.

AgentTrove was previously added as a DataKit source in #7766, with trajectories rendered as role-tagged documents. I'd like to investigate whether the current representation preserves the chat/tool-use structure needed for mid-training, and identify any changes required to make the data suitable for Levanter training.

## Proposed work

1. **Audit the current AgentTrove pipeline:** Review how trajectories are normalized, rendered, and tokenized. Check preservation of message roles, tool calls/responses, turn boundaries, termination markers, and outcome metadata.
2. **Validate chat-template compatibility:** Compare the existing representation against the intended model/tokenizer chat template. Identify any formatting mismatches or information loss.
3. **Implement and test changes if needed:** Add or modify DataKit processing and validation tests, with a small reproducible sample demonstrating the resulting training representation.
4. **Explore downstream experiments:** If useful, design a small-scale training comparison to test whether improved formatting affects tool-use behavior. This would be scoped separately depending on available compute.

## Definition of done

- Document the existing AgentTrove representation and any identified formatting issues.
- Establish a validated, reproducible path from AgentTrove trajectories to the intended training representation.
- Add appropriate tests for role boundaries, tool-call formatting, and termination handling.
- Submit a PR for any required changes

## Open questions

- Which target chat template/model should this initially support?
- Are there existing changes or experiments addressing this that I should build on?
- Would a smaller-scale training ablation be useful after validating the data pipeline?

I'm happy to take ownership of the initial audit/validation and coordinate on the implementation scope before starting.

## References

- Existing AgentTrove DataKit integration: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7766
- Marin contribution guidelines: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/explanations/guidelines.md

spillover_issues.author: gonzalobenegas
spillover_issues.body:
Integrate the original 5,200-question [GenomeQA benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05774) through **TaskCompendium** (PR #10984): six biological subtasks, one answer per question, no tools or retrieval. The PR targets `main` after evaluation migration #10957 merged and reuses its corpus pipeline. Reporting, public launcher access, and official-policy admission remain separate.

Decisions:

| Topic | Agreed approach and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Data | Use pinned `HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa` binary-choice (BCQ) and multiple-choice (MCQ) data. All 5,200 evaluation rows match the author release. Exclude Carbon’s modified tasks and subsets. |
| Reporting | Foreground the six biological subtask scores and their overall mean. Within each subtask, average BCQ and MCQ equally; then average the six subtasks equally. This prevents the smaller motif task from being underweighted. Retain BCQ/MCQ summaries, all 12 cells, denominators, and ordinary correct counts. No chance correction. |
| Prompt | Use the fixed optimized prompt from the public runner. Optimization already happened offline; no new prompt search. Fetch the pinned prompt externally without executing upstream code or bundling the prompt in Marin. |
| Generation | Temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.95, matching the released runner. Shared total cap of 16,384 generated tokens, including reasoning, visible analysis, and the answer. Enable thinking where supported; pin effort and verify token-budget semantics per provider. |
| Implementation | Reuse TaskCompendium acquisition, task conversion, source-grader packaging, and evaluation protocols. Retain the small GenomeQA parser, per-cell weights, and subtask/format groups. Add final-only response selection; do not add a custom runner or reducer. |
| Grading | Grade final content only. Reject ambiguous/invalid options; unparseable and length-truncated answers score zero. Transport failures remain ungraded. Retain the agreed parser; recovering observed formatting failures would add only 0.0167 percentage points. |
| Asset handling | Reuse licenses remain unspecified. Keep questions and responses in controlled storage, tests synthetic, and public reports aggregate-only. External fetching does not resolve use terms. |

Additional Snowball-cohort validation: **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is complete in both modes, with 5,200/5,200 graded each. Thinking-on scores 45.58% versus 44.35% off (+1.23 percentage points). GPT-OSS-20B low-effort is also complete at 47.08%.** These are single-seed, fixed-protocol comparisons. GPT-OSS has no true thinking-off setting; it uses the cohort's `reasoning_effort: low` convention.

| Biological subtask | Qwen thinking-off | Qwen thinking-on | GPT-OSS low-effort |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer vs. promoter | 47.20% | 50.40% | 48.90% |
| Splice sites | 29.70% | 32.00% | 37.70% |
| Species classification | 50.00% | 50.20% | 49.90% |
| Histone marks | 40.40% | 38.80% | 39.70% |
| Transcription-factor binding sites | 41.80% | 42.60% | 46.30% |
| Motifs | 57.00% | 59.50% | 60.00% |
| **Six-subtask macro** | **44.35%** | **45.58%** | **47.08%** |

Qwen thinking improves five of six subtask macros, with histone marks down 1.60 points. BCQ improves **51.87% → 54.03%**; MCQ changes **36.83% → 37.13%**. The modest overall gain accompanies **2.08× output tokens** (13,909,197 → 28,897,134) and more truncations: **318/5,200 (6.12%) → 393/5,200 (7.56%)**. Both modes have zero parsing failures and zero separately classified refusals. This is sensitivity to thinking mode under the same 16,384-token cap, not a claim of statistical significance or model-optimal settings. Gemma's thinking-on decline therefore does not generalize uniformly to Qwen under this protocol.

GPT-OSS BCQ/MCQ macros are **53.77% / 40.40%**, with **34 truncations (0.65%)**, zero parsing failures, and zero separately classified refusals. Truncations score zero in the full-population denominator for every run.

All three cohort runs are complete and their serving resources stopped. Qwen's native retries recovered 62 first-pass infrastructure failures in off mode and 28 in on mode. The GPT-OSS recovery completed all 142 outstanding questions and verified that all 5,058 prior responses and grades are hash-identical. No benchmark-code change was needed for recovery.

<details>
<summary>Cohort protocol, usage, artifacts, and operational findings</summary>

Qwen thinking-on job `/exedev/genomeqa-qwen-on-20261116` ran from November 16 at 23:25 UTC to November 17 by 01:25 UTC, within its four-H100, four-hour bound (at most 16 H100-hours). It retained the same pinned model/runtime, all 5,200 questions, sampling, seed, concurrency, and 16,384-token total output cap. Preflight verified byte-identical question shards and protocol equality except `enable_thinking: true`. A saved request independently confirmed that switch, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and max output 16,384. Final audit confirmed 5,200 unique graded samples, all 12 expected cell sizes, and token usage for exactly 5,200 graded attempts. The 28 first-pass infrastructure failures recovered through the native retry; successful answers were skipped. The serving context closed before aggregation, parent succeeded, worker and broker stopped, and a fresh regional snapshot had no matching pods. Final graded-attempt usage: 7,644,074 input and 28,897,134 output tokens. Output includes reasoning and final-answer tokens; no separate split or total failed-attempt cost is claimed. Artifacts under `qwen-on/`: `scores.json`, `usage.json`, `completed.json`, `preflight.json`, and `recorded-request-check.json`. `qwen-thinking-comparison.json` at the cohort root contains the paired aggregate comparison. GPT-OSS medium effort remains an unlaunched follow-up.

Both use the pinned cohort checkpoints, runtime `fe813e34c2`, native TaskCompendium/Marin runner, 5,200 original questions, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, seed 42, concurrency 64, and a 16,384-token total output cap. Qwen uses `enable_thinking: false`; GPT-OSS uses `reasoning_effort: low`. Rendered-template checks passed before GPU allocation. GPT-OSS's separately published protocol retains byte-identical task/evaluation shards. Other generation settings retain checkpoint/server defaults; these are fixed GenomeQA-protocol runs, not runs of each model's full recommended sampling recipe.

Qwen revision: `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`, four H100s, TP2 × DP2. GPT-OSS revision: `6cee5e81ee83917806bbde320786a8fb61efebee`, one H100. Each parent had a two-hour bound. Qwen's final graded-attempt usage is 7,654,474 input and 13,909,197 output tokens. The original GPT-OSS partial run's 5,058 graded attempts used 7,601,434 input and 7,731,110 output tokens; these are not full-run totals and exclude the later 142 recovered answers. These totals exclude failed attempts; output includes visible analysis and any reasoning, without a separate reasoning-token count.

Jobs: `/exedev/genomeqa-qwen-off-20261116` and `/exedev/genomeqa-gptoss-low-20261116`. GPT-OSS initially waited about 31 minutes for GPU capacity. Regional task events subsequently showed broker preemptions at 19:44 and 20:03 UTC, and GPU-worker preemption at 19:54:59 UTC. The worker requeued without obtaining another GPU before cancellation. The client retained pending responses while the serving worker had no active requests; the hub's running status was stale. All three tasks have termination events at 20:12:10 UTC, and a fresh regional backend snapshot contains no matching pods. These are infrastructure losses, not scored model failures. A subsequent recovery, `/exedev/genomeqa-gptoss-recovery-20261116`, was bounded to one H100 and one hour (20:27–21:27 UTC). The GPU worker remained SchedulingGated throughout because GPU/RDMA quota was unavailable; no new answers were generated. A saved-result audit at 21:15 UTC verified all 5,058 graded responses unchanged and 142 still outstanding. The recovery was cancelled at its deadline; parent, broker, and worker termination events were recorded at 21:27:25 UTC. A second authorized one-hour recovery, `/exedev/genomeqa-gptoss-recovery2-20261116`, submitted at 22:05 UTC, obtained GPU capacity promptly and succeeded by 22:34 UTC. Its first pass recovered 141 questions and the next native pass recovered the last question. The final audit verified 5,200 unique graded questions, all 12 expected cell sizes, and zero changes to the original 5,058 graded responses. Serving closed before scoring; the worker and broker are stopped, and a fresh regional snapshot contains no matching pods.

Native retry incurred a full-population selection scan before the remaining requests, which added substantial overhead. The original launcher requested zero worker failure/preemption retries, but the broker had separate nonzero retry defaults. The recovery explicitly set both worker and broker retry limits to zero. The original worker nevertheless requeued after preemption despite its zero limit; that discrepancy remains unresolved and was not patched in the benchmark PR.

Aggregate root: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/cohort-fe813e34-20261116/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fcohort-fe813e34-20261116%2F). Qwen: `qwen-off/scores.json`, `usage.json`, `completed.json`. GPT-OSS final artifacts: `gptoss-low/scores.json`, `completed.json`, and `recovery-preservation.json`. Historical `monitor-before-deadline.json`, `preserved-graded-hashes.json`, and `recovery-progress.json` retain the 5,058-result baseline and the earlier capacity-blocked attempt. Raw questions/responses remain in controlled storage. No dashboard ingestion is claimed.

</details>

Gemma validation (2026-11-16): **Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it is complete in both modes: 5,200/5,200 graded each. Thinking-off macro is 44.08%; thinking-on is 39.12% (−4.97 percentage points).** The final one-question retry succeeded; all 5,199 previously graded thinking-on responses and grades are hash-identical. The parent succeeded and the model worker and broker are stopped.

| Biological subtask | Thinking off | Thinking on | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer vs. promoter | 38.60% | 36.30% | -2.30 pp |
| Splice sites | 37.30% | 23.40% | -13.90 pp |
| Species classification | 47.10% | 34.90% | -12.20 pp |
| Histone marks | 40.70% | 31.70% | -9.00 pp |
| Transcription-factor binding sites | 41.80% | 39.40% | -2.40 pp |
| Motifs | 59.00% | 69.00% | +10.00 pp |
| **Six-subtask macro** | **44.08%** | **39.12%** | **−4.97 pp** |

BCQ macro: **54.43% → 49.47%**. MCQ macro: **33.73% → 28.77%**. Thinking improves motifs (+10 pp), but lowers all five other subtask macros under this protocol. This is a single-seed comparison at the same 16,384-token total output cap, not evidence that thinking is universally worse.

Thinking-off has **12/5,200 truncations (0.23%)**; thinking-on has **1,341/5,200 (25.79%)**. Both have zero parsing failures or separately classified refusals. Truncations score zero in the full-population denominator. The largest thinking-on truncation rates are splice-site MCQ (316/500, 63.2%) and species MCQ (262/500, 52.4%). Truncation is a major confound in interpreting underlying task ability; the aggregate alone cannot isolate its causal contribution.

Generated tokens: **1,436,334 off vs. 47,058,415 on (32.76×)**, or **276 vs. 9,050 per question**. These are total output tokens, including thinking, not a measured reasoning/final-answer split; they cover the final graded attempts rather than all failed-attempt or startup costs. Input tokens: 7,298,523 off; 7,288,123 on.

[Aggregate artifact in Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fgemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112%2Ffinal-thinking-comparison.json) · `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/gemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112/final-thinking-comparison.json`. These are diagnostic aggregates computed from native FineStore results; dashboard ingestion is not claimed.

<details>
<summary>Completed continuation and retry history</summary>

All continuations retained runtime `fe813e34c2`, model revision, prompts, sampling, and output cap. The initial private concurrency override was 32; the user approved switching to Marin's native default of 64. Resume identity excludes concurrency. The first concurrency-64 submission was blocked by the shared Iris federation transfer-budget failure and cancelled without starting. After controller recovery, the November 13 two-hour continuation reached 5,199/5,200 before timeout; its children stopped automatically. The November 16 final retry was limited to two H100s for 30 minutes and completed in about 20 minutes, including model startup and native resume bookkeeping. Exactly one model response was generated (16,384 output tokens); it truncated and scored zero. The final audit verified complete graded coverage and preservation of all 5,199 prior on-mode answers. Prior audits also verified preservation of the original 5,091 off-mode answers. No core retry or scoring change was required.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Recovery decisions and earlier failure</summary>

Before recovery: **Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it thinking-off is partial: 5,091 graded / 5,200, with 109 model-connection failures (`APIConnectionError`); thinking-on has not run.** The corrected cluster-only submission passed model preparation and generated answers through TaskCompendium and Marin/vLLM. The runner then raised `EvaluationInfrastructureError`; its serving worker and broker are stopped. FineStore preserves successful grades and failed-attempt evidence for recovery. Do not report the available-grade aggregate as a complete benchmark score. Recorded usage for the completed responses: 7,145,508 input and 1,392,082 output tokens. After explicit authorization to fix the failed run, recovery job `/exedev/genomeqa-gemma-recovery-20261113` was submitted on November 13. The private launcher now calls the existing `execute_with_retries` wrapper (up to three native passes per mode) instead of single-pass `execute`. Successful attempts are skipped on resume; hashes of the 5,091 graded responses were saved for verification. The model, protocol, seed, cap, and concurrency are unchanged. This recovery is bounded to two H100s for two hours (at most four additional H100-hours); no core-code change or unbounded resubmission was added. The lower-level cause of the connection failures remains unconfirmed.

</details>

Both modes were prepared with a 16,384-token total output cap, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, seed 42, and the checkpoint’s top-k 64 default. CPU preparation and the pinned tokenizer’s thinking-switch check passed; both published inputs contain byte-identical question/evaluation shards for all 5,200 questions. Both modes used two-H100 serving allocations; completed answers were retained across bounded continuations. Truncations remain zero-scored. This measures a policy-relevant open-weight model, not paper parity.

<details>
<summary>Paired Gemma run provenance</summary>

Model revision: `4d7ae4984b7db7de8f8457170b3f1a419ee76d52`; adapter/runtime revision: `fe813e34c2`. Reuse the existing cohort model configuration, compilation and CUDA graphs, corpus publication, native evaluation worker, packaged grader, and FineStore. Separate corpus protocols change only `enable_thinking`; the same questions, prompt, generation cap, and aggregation apply to both. Unlike the earlier SimpleQA example’s 2,048/16,384 split, equal caps avoid confounding thinking with output allowance. No new public launcher or core code is added. Raw artifacts remain controlled; publish only audited aggregates.

Iris replacement job: `/exedev/genomeqa-gemma-paired-r2-20261113`. The original job was cancelled before GPU inference: the private launcher incorrectly constrained the region to `US-EAST-02A`, producing a node selector that excluded all 36 nodes. The corrected submission uses cluster-only placement, matching the standard launcher. Both original jobs were confirmed stopped. The replacement retains the original 2026-11-13 02:22 UTC deadline rather than resetting its four-hour allowance. A submitted job is not a completed or scored benchmark. Audit selection and grading counts, reasoning/final separation, truncations, parse failures, and all twelve cells before reporting full results. Preserve partial FineStore artifacts if the time bound is reached; do not silently extend the budget.

</details>

Historical model validation (2026-11-06, **Evalchemy path**):

**Llama-4 Maverick completed all 5,200 questions through native Evalchemy and FineStore.** All 12 cell counts and macro aggregation were checked. Combined macro: **50.60%**, versus **49.07%** derived from the paper’s BCQ/MCQ results. BCQ: **57.43%**; MCQ: **43.77%**. Unweighted accuracy: **47.46% (2,468/5,200)**.

| Biological subtask | Paper combined | Run combined | Difference (percentage points) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer/promoter | 45.70% | 46.70% | +1.00 |
| Splice sites | 38.00% | 37.50% | −0.50 |
| Taxonomy | 56.60% | 61.90% | +5.30 |
| Histone marks | 42.10% | 42.90% | +0.80 |
| TFBS | 43.00% | 43.60% | +0.60 |
| Motifs | 69.00% | 71.00% | +2.00 |
| Overall macro | 49.07% | 50.60% | +1.53 |

Combined paper values are derived from [Table 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05774v1#S4.T2). This is a development comparison, not exact replication: providers, precision, stochastic sampling, parser, and explicit output cap can differ.

There were **six parse failures, no scored refusals, and no output-limit truncations**. Maverick had no separate thinking control enabled, consistent with its paper configuration; the prompt still requests visible analysis. Reported API cost was **$3.08** (conservative accounting bound **$3.93**), excluding CPU hosting and the connectivity pilot.

TaskCompendium migration validation (2026-11-12, `fe813e34c2`): **all 5,200 saved requests and responses were replayed with zero prompt, per-item metric, or extracted-answer differences**. All **120 grouped metric comparisons** match, preserving the full-run results above. This reuses the existing generation run; it is not a new full-benchmark run.

A separate **two-question live native smoke** (one BCQ, one MCQ; Maverick/Parasail FP8) completed through the published corpus, context selection, ChatModel, RolloutEngine, isolated packaged grader, and FineStore. Both attempts were graded without parsing or infrastructure failures. Usage: **1,982 input + 348 output tokens**, zero reported reasoning tokens; API cost **$0.0010417**, excluding CPU hosting. No retries or GPUs were used for inference. The same two-question path also passed a no-cost preflight using saved HTTP responses.

<details>
<summary>Migration validation scope and execution differences</summary>

The replay compared current messages with both historical HTTP requests and FineStore samples, selected final content, and checked every stored metric and extracted answer. Six historical parse failures remain unchanged. Group comparisons cover six metrics across the six subtasks, two formats, and twelve cells.

The live wire sent seed 42 and `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": true}`; the historical OpenRouter calls omitted both. Temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and the 16,384-token cap match. Sending these fields does not prove provider enforcement or hidden-reasoning support. The smoke validates execution, not score parity or statistical performance.

The smoke used the standard BASIC_GRADER lock builder and the pinned tokenizer loaded with `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`. `AutoTokenizer` failed on a field-type mismatch in the pinned model configuration; therefore the automatic launcher/tokenizer-loading path is not validated. Public launcher access, dashboard ingestion, and production reporting remain separate. No implementation changes were needed for replay or smoke validation.

Setup-only attempts encountered an omitted input file and unintended Iris child-worker selection during publication; they made no model requests and were stopped. The successful CPU job used the already-published corpus, made exactly two model requests, and finished with archived outputs verified. Raw evidence remains private.

TaskCompendium validation (2026-11-10): **all 5,200 pinned questions pass conversion and reference-answer grading**, with correct cell populations, equal cell weights, and an unchanged prompt hash. All **23 GenomeQA tests** pass, including native publication and fixed-budget selection. The TaskCompendium suite passed **714 tests (4 skipped)** before the declaration-only sampling fix. Lint passes and all advisory findings are addressed. Another **103 integration tests** passed, and TaskCompendium’s typecheck reports **zero errors**.
